From July 2025, Aussies can save 30% on solar battery systems. This post explains what the Australian Government's Cheaper Home Batteries Program is, who is eligible, how the rebate works alongside state incentives, and what it means for households, businesses and the wider energy industry. It also introduces GreenCharge, our dedicated platform for battery guidance.

What is the Cheaper Home Batteries Program?

Starting 1 July 2025, the Australian Government rolled out the Cheaper Home Batteries Program, a $2.3 billion initiative designed to make clean energy storage more accessible. Under this program, households, small businesses and community facilities can access a 30% discount on the upfront cost of installing eligible small-scale solar battery systems (5 kWh to 50 kWh capacity).

The incentive is delivered through the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme (SRES) and will gradually taper off until 2030, encouraging early adoption. The Government's target is ambitious: to install over one million new batteries by 2030.

Why this matters

For households

  • Big savings: existing solar owners could reduce their energy bills by up to AUD 2,600 per year. Those who add both solar and batteries may save as much as AUD 6,000 annually, potentially reducing a typical family's electricity costs by up to 90%.
  • Energy independence: store your daytime solar power for use in the evenings, reducing reliance on fluctuating grid prices.
  • Long-term payback: even after rebates taper, battery technology is becoming cheaper, meaning today's investment sets households up for future-proof energy savings.

For the grid and climate

  • Grid resilience: batteries smooth out peak demand, such as summer evenings when air-conditioners spike usage.
  • Reduced emissions: more storage means less reliance on coal and gas during high-demand periods.
  • Support for renewables: solar is already Australia's most popular renewable; batteries are the missing link that makes it reliable around the clock. The Government's announcement, Discounted batteries for households through the Cheaper Home Batteries Program, sets out the details.

Who is eligible and key details

  • Eligible recipients: households, small businesses and community facilities, with existing or new solar.
  • Battery criteria: usable capacity between 5 kWh and 100 kWh, with rebates applying up to 50 kWh. The battery must be CEC-accredited, Virtual Power Plant (VPP)-capable, and installed by an SAA-accredited installer.
  • One rebate per site: only one rebate per household or per business meter.
  • Program delivery: rebates are applied at the point of sale via accredited retailers and installers, so there is no separate claim form for the homeowner to lodge.

State programs and stacking incentives

Australia already has several state-level incentives for batteries, and these can often be combined with the federal program for greater savings:

  • Victoria: Solar Homes Program battery rebate (up to $2,950).
  • South Australia: Virtual Power Plant schemes offering discounted batteries.
  • New South Wales: Empowering Homes program with zero-interest loans.
  • Queensland: a solar battery rebate pilot was announced for 2024.

Households should check federal and state programs together to maximise benefits, and confirm current terms before signing, as state schemes change over time.

What it means for industry

  • Solar retailers and installers: expect strong demand growth, requiring a scale-up of the certified workforce.
  • Battery manufacturers: Australia could become a priority market, driving competition and lowering prices further.
  • Virtual Power Plants (VPPs): as more households join VPPs, grid operators can tap into distributed storage, reducing blackouts and stabilising supply.

How to apply

The Cheaper Home Batteries Program represents more than just cost savings. It is a landmark shift in how Australians generate, store and use energy.

For households:

  1. Check eligibility. Do you have solar, or are you planning a new installation?
  2. Select accredited products and installers. Compliance ensures safety and eligibility for rebates.
  3. Explore VPPs. Join a network to earn bill credits or payments for sharing stored energy back to the grid.

For businesses, batteries can reduce overhead costs and enhance sustainability credentials, which is essential in ESG reporting and in achieving carbon targets.

Explore more with GreenCharge

To help households and businesses make the most of the Cheaper Home Batteries Program, we have launched our new dedicated platform, GreenCharge. There you will find clear guidance on eligibility, accredited products, and how to maximise your savings by combining federal and state rebates. We have shared this blog across our wider network to raise awareness, but GreenCharge is the go-to hub for the latest tools, resources and expert insights tailored to Australians ready to take the next step in their clean energy journey.

Final thought

This program is not just about cleaner energy. It is about empowering Australians to take control of their energy future. With falling technology costs, generous incentives and growing climate urgency, now is the perfect time to invest in solar batteries. By 2030, a million homes and businesses could be powered by stored solar energy, reducing bills, easing grid strain and driving Australia closer to its net-zero goals.

Greenhse Technologies in Perth has supplied energy-efficient LED lighting and smart home products for many years, and a home battery is a natural next step for customers who have already cut their lighting load. If you would like to talk through your options, visit us at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 or call (08) 9297 2969.

/blog/bad-lighting-easy-solution.html.bodyHtml:
When your existing lighting just isn't good enough for working from home, changing it is as easy as 1, 2, 3. This post explains why the lighting in many Perth homes lets people down once a spare room becomes an office, what to change, how simple the swap to LED downlights really is, and what a licensed electrician does on the day. Click on the video link below to see just how easy it is.

Why old lighting fails for working from home

Most bedrooms and spare rooms were lit for sleeping and getting dressed, not for eight hours in front of a screen. A single pendant or oyster fitting in the middle of the ceiling gives a soft, warm pool of light directly below it and leaves the desk against the wall in shadow. Once you sit at that desk you are working in your own shadow, squinting at documents and relying on the monitor to light your face on video calls.

Older halogen and incandescent fittings add other problems. They are usually a very warm colour, around the yellow end of the scale, which feels cosy at night but makes it harder to stay alert during the day. They produce a lot of heat, which matters in a small closed room over a Perth summer. They also cost far more to run than LED and the lamps fail regularly, so you end up with one or two globes out and the room even darker than before.

The usual symptoms are easy to recognise:

  • Tired, dry eyes and headaches by mid-afternoon.
  • Glare on the screen from a single bright globe behind or above you.
  • A dim, patchy room that looks dull on video calls.
  • Rising power bills from lights that stay on all day.

What to change

The easy solution is to replace the single central fitting with a small number of LED downlights spread evenly across the ceiling. Downlights put light where you need it, over the desk and the rest of the room, instead of in one spot. Because each fitting is low wattage you can run several of them for less energy than one old halogen.

When choosing downlights for a home office, a few general points help:

  • Colour temperature: a neutral or cool white, roughly 4000K to 5000K, feels closer to daylight and suits concentration. Many LED downlights are switchable between warm, neutral and cool white so you can pick the setting once installed.
  • Even spacing: a wide beam angle and even spacing across the ceiling removes the dark corners and reduces shadows on the desk.
  • Low glare: a recessed LED source with a diffuser or deeper reflector is far kinder on the eyes than a bare globe.
  • Dimming: a dimmable fitting lets you turn the room down for evening work or video calls.

Watch the short clip to see the before and after for yourself: Watch the bad lighting, easy solution video.

The swap is as easy as 1, 2, 3

Replacing a ceiling light with LED downlights sounds like a renovation, but for a standard plasterboard ceiling with roof space above it is a quick job. The process is:

  1. Plan the layout. Decide how many downlights the room needs and mark the positions on the ceiling, keeping them clear of ceiling joists and spacing them evenly with the desk area well covered.
  2. Cut the holes. A hole saw of the correct size cuts a clean opening for each downlight in the plasterboard.
  3. Connect and clip in. Each downlight is wired to the lighting circuit, the spring clips are folded back, and the fitting is pushed up into the hole where it sits flush with the ceiling.

The old central fitting is removed and its cable is reused or made safe. Most single rooms can be done in a couple of hours, with very little dust and no repainting needed.

What a licensed electrician does

In Western Australia any work on 240V fixed wiring, including installing downlights, must be carried out by a licensed electrician. Beyond the legal requirement, the electrician brings the parts of the job that a homeowner cannot safely do:

  • Isolates the lighting circuit at the switchboard and tests that it is dead before starting.
  • Checks the roof space for insulation, other cables and services before cutting the ceiling, and confirms the downlights are rated for contact with insulation where needed.
  • Runs new cable between the downlight positions and terminates every connection correctly.
  • Installs a dimmer or replacement switch if you choose dimmable fittings.
  • Tests the circuit, confirms the earth and RCD protection, and supplies a certificate of electrical safety for the work.

You can watch the process from start to finish in our second video showing the LED downlight installation.

Wrap-up

Poor lighting is one of the cheapest home office problems to fix. A handful of LED downlights, laid out properly and installed by a licensed electrician, turns a gloomy spare room into a bright, comfortable workspace and lowers the running cost at the same time. If you are working from home in Perth and want help choosing the right downlights, colour temperature and dimming for your room, visit Greenhse Technologies at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069, or call (08) 9297 2969 and we will point you to the easy solution.

/blog/best-smart-home-devices-australia..bodyHtml:
Smart home technology is no longer a futuristic dream. It is here and more accessible than ever. From managing your lighting with a few taps on your smartphone or a simple voice command, to keeping your home secure with cameras and smart sensors, these devices simplify daily life, save energy and can even increase your home's value. But how do you choose the right products for your Australian home?

What are smart home devices?

Have you seen trouble while adding a Bluetooth Gateway smart light connection? Many Perth customers buy Bluetooth smart lights, switches or garden controllers, then find that the lights only work while their phone is in the room. The missing piece is a Bluetooth Mesh Gateway. This guide explains what the gateway does, why you need one, and the step-by-step process of connecting your Bluetooth Mesh Gateway to the Smart Life app. We also have a short video that walks through the same steps.

What a Bluetooth Mesh Gateway does

Bluetooth smart devices talk directly to your phone over a short range. That is fine for a single lamp, but it has limits: your phone has to be nearby, and there is no way to reach the device from outside the house. A Bluetooth Mesh Gateway solves this. It is a small, low-power hub that sits between your Bluetooth devices and your WiFi router, giving them a path to the internet.

Once the gateway is set up, your Tuya and Smart Life Bluetooth devices gain the same features as WiFi devices:

  • Remote control from anywhere with mobile data.
  • Schedules and timers that run even when your phone is switched off.
  • Voice control through Amazon Alexa and Google Home.
  • Automations that link Bluetooth lights to other smart devices in the app.

The word "mesh" matters too. In a Bluetooth mesh network every device passes messages on to its neighbours, so the signal hops from light to light rather than relying on one central point. Multiple mesh nodes work at the same time, giving wide coverage and strong resistance to interference. The more mesh lights you have, the stronger the network becomes.

What you need before you start

  • The Bluetooth Mesh Gateway and its USB power lead and plug.
  • A 2.4GHz WiFi network. Most smart home gateways do not connect to 5GHz bands, so if your router combines both under one name, connect your phone to the 2.4GHz network first or split the bands in your router settings.
  • Your WiFi password.
  • The Smart Life app installed on your phone, with an account created and logged in. The Tuya Smart app works in exactly the same way.
  • Bluetooth and location permission turned on for the app. Android and iOS both require location access to scan for nearby Bluetooth devices.

Choose a central spot for the gateway, within WiFi range of your router and Bluetooth range of at least one smart device. A hallway or living area usually works well.

Step-by-step: adding the gateway in the Smart Life app

  1. Plug the gateway in. The indicator lights on the top of the unit will come on. Wait a few seconds for it to boot.
  2. Put the gateway into pairing mode. Press and hold the small button on the side of the unit for about five seconds until the indicator starts flashing quickly. A rapid flash means the gateway is ready to be discovered. If it flashes slowly, press and hold again until it changes to a fast flash.
  3. Open the Smart Life app and tap the plus symbol in the top right corner, then choose Add Device.
  4. The app will usually find the gateway automatically and show it at the top of the screen under devices to be added. Tap Add. If it does not appear, select Gateway Control from the category list on the left and choose the Bluetooth Gateway option.
  5. Select your 2.4GHz WiFi network, enter the password and confirm.
  6. Wait while the app connects. The progress bar will move through three stages: finding the device, registering it to the cloud and initialising. This normally takes under a minute.
  7. When the gateway appears as Added Successfully, give it a sensible name such as Downstairs Gateway and choose the room it lives in. Tap Done.

Prefer to see it done on screen? Watch the connection video at the top of this post, which follows exactly the same sequence.

Adding Bluetooth lights and devices to the gateway

With the gateway online, your Bluetooth devices can be linked to it in two ways.

  • New devices: open the gateway in the app, tap Add Sub-device, then put the light or switch into pairing mode (usually by switching it on and off three times, or holding its reset button). The gateway will search, find and add it.
  • Devices already in the app: Bluetooth devices that were added directly to your phone are usually migrated to the gateway automatically once both are in the same home in the app. If one is not, remove it and add it again through the gateway.

Sub-devices connected through the gateway can be grouped, scheduled and added to scenes like any WiFi device, and respond to Alexa and Google voice commands once your Smart Life account is linked to that assistant.

Troubleshooting common problems

  • Gateway not found: confirm your phone is on 2.4GHz WiFi with Bluetooth on, and that the indicator is flashing fast. Move the phone closer to the gateway during pairing.
  • Stuck at registering to the cloud: the WiFi password was probably typed incorrectly, or the router is blocking new devices. Re-enter the password and check any MAC filtering or guest network limits.
  • Devices drop offline: the gateway may be too far from the nearest mesh light. Move it closer, or add another mesh device between the two so the signal can hop across.
  • Need to start again: hold the side button until the indicator flashes quickly. This resets the gateway so it can be paired afresh.

Getting help in Perth

A Bluetooth Mesh Gateway is a small addition that turns a handful of Bluetooth lights into a proper smart home system with remote access, scheduling and voice control. If you are still having trouble with your Bluetooth Gateway smart light connection, the team at Greenhse Technologies in Perth is happy to help. Visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 or phone (08) 9297 2969.

/blog/brilliant-warranty-repair.html.bodyHtml:
Are you tired of dealing with complicated warranty repair processes? Look no further. Brilliant have advised that in case of warranty repairs you need to lodge a support call and they will send a technician to investigate. This post explains how the Brilliant warranty repair process works for ceiling fans and lighting bought through Greenhse Technologies in Perth, what documents and photos you need to have ready, and how to contact Brilliant directly so the claim moves as quickly as possible.

How the Brilliant warranty repair process works

The warranty repair process is designed to be easy, hassle-free and, most importantly, reliable. Brilliant ceiling fans and light fittings are installed permanently by an electrician, so rather than asking you to take the product down and return it, Brilliant handle warranty repairs through a support call. Once the call is lodged, they arrange for a technician to visit, investigate the fault and repair or replace the unit as needed.

The process begins with a simple call or email to the customer service team. They will guide you through the necessary steps and assist at every stage. Their expert technicians will promptly diagnose and fix any issues as soon as possible. You can read the full warranty terms and lodge a claim on the Brilliant Lighting warranty page.

What you will need before you lodge a claim

Brilliant need to confirm two things before they send a technician: that the product is within its warranty period, and that it was installed correctly by a licensed electrician. Faults caused by incorrect installation are not covered, which is why installation evidence is requested. Have the following ready:

  1. Proof of purchase. Your Greenhse Technologies invoice or receipt showing the product and the purchase date. If you have lost it, contact us and we can look it up for you.
  2. Evidence of licensed installation. One of the following is enough:
    • A copy of the electrical certificate of compliance, provided by the electrician when he installed the units.
    • OR a copy of the electrician's electrical licence.
    • OR a copy of the invoice from your electrician for the installation of the fans.
  3. Photos of the installation. You will need to send a photo of the fan installation and the wall isolating switch as well, and sometimes they ask for a photo of the remote (front and back).

The photo of the wall isolating switch shows that the fan has its own means of isolation, as required for a compliant installation. The photo of the remote, front and back, lets the support team identify the receiver and remote model and check for pairing or battery issues before a technician is sent.

Contacting Brilliant

You could also send an email first to see if they know what the problem is. Many faults, such as a fan that will not respond to the remote or a light that flickers on one setting, have known causes, and the support team may be able to talk you through a fix without a site visit. Email Brilliant Lighting support with a short description of the fault, the product name, your proof of purchase and the photos listed above.

You can contact them by phone on 03 9765 2555. Note that this is Eastern States time, so Brilliant's office hours run two or three hours ahead of Perth depending on daylight saving. Calling before lunchtime Perth time gives you the best chance of reaching someone the same day.

Tips for a smooth claim

  • Keep your Greenhse invoice and your electrician's certificate of compliance together in one place from the day of installation. They are the two documents every warranty claim needs.
  • Do not remove or dismantle the fan or light before the technician visits. Warranty work is carried out on the installed unit.
  • Describe the fault clearly: when it started, whether it happens on every speed or setting, and whether the wall switch or remote is used. This helps the technician arrive with the right parts.
  • Take the photos in good light so the model label, wiring cover and switch are easy to read.
  • If the product was installed by an electrician you found through Greenhse, we may be able to help you obtain a copy of the installation invoice.

Where Greenhse fits in

Greenhse Technologies supplies Brilliant fans and lighting, but the manufacturer's warranty is administered by Brilliant themselves. That is why the claim goes to their support team rather than back to our showroom. We are still here to help: we can confirm your purchase details, reissue an invoice, explain which document Brilliant are asking for, and advise whether the symptom you are seeing is a warranty matter or an installation issue for your electrician.

Lodging a Brilliant warranty repair is straightforward once you have your proof of purchase, evidence of licensed installation and a few photos ready. For any help with a Brilliant product bought from us, or advice on fans and lighting for your home, contact Greenhse Technologies in Perth on (08) 9297 2969 or visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069.

/blog/choose-led-ceiling-lights-perth-ho.lede: Discover how to choose the perfect LED ceiling lights for your Perth home. Explore lighting types, room-specific tips, energy efficiency, and design ideas to brighten your space the smart way.
/blog/choose-led-ceiling-lights-perth-ho.bodyHtml:
Lighting can make or break the atmosphere in your home. Whether you're setting the mood in the living room, improving home appearance, or enhancing the functionality of your kitchen, choosing the right LED ceiling lights is key. This guide explains the main types of LED ceiling lights, how to match them to each room, and how to get size, lumens and colour temperature right.

For Perth homeowners looking to upgrade or build, Greenhse Technologies offers a wide range of high-quality ceiling, panel and oyster lights tailored to modern Australian homes.

Why LED ceiling lighting is the smart choice

LED ceiling lighting has revolutionised the way we light our homes. Compared to traditional incandescent or fluorescent lighting, LED ceiling lights offer:

  • Up to 80% energy savings
  • Longer lifespan (25,000 to 50,000 hours)
  • Better brightness with lower power use
  • Minimal heat output
  • Eco-friendly performance with no toxic materials

If you're investing in lighting for your Perth home, LED ceiling lights are the most efficient and cost-effective solution.

The main types of LED ceiling lights

1. Ceiling lights in Perth

General-purpose fixtures mounted directly to the ceiling, perfect for bedrooms, kitchens and hallways. They suit homes with lower ceilings where pendant lights would hang too low.

2. Panel lights in Perth

Panel lights provide uniform, diffused light over a wider area, making them ideal for living rooms, dining areas, offices and open-plan spaces. They also work well in false ceilings.

3. Oyster lights in Perth

Oyster lights are surface-mounted, round fixtures with a clean, minimalist appearance. They are a top choice for bathrooms, hallways and utility spaces. Oyster lights from Greenhse Technologies Perth combine design, efficiency and long-term performance, with slim-profile designs suited to contemporary homes.

Match the lighting to the room

Each room has a unique purpose, so the lighting should match its function:

  • Living room: panel lights with adjustable brightness and colour temperature for layering ambience.
  • Kitchen: ceiling lights on a cool white setting for clear, bright visibility while cooking.
  • Bedroom: warm white ceiling lights or dimmable options for a relaxing feel.
  • Bathroom: moisture-resistant oyster lights with neutral to cool white light.
  • Office: panel lights with neutral white light to reduce eye strain and improve focus.

Choose the right size and mounting style

When selecting LED ceiling lights in Perth, the size and wattage of the light play a crucial role in balanced, efficient lighting. The wrong size leaves areas too dim or too bright, affecting both looks and function.

Small rooms or low ceilings (2.4m to 2.7m)

Flush-mounted or compact ceiling lights are ideal for bedrooms, hallways and laundry areas.

Medium-sized rooms (bedrooms, studies, dining areas)

Medium-wattage LED ceiling lights provide enough brightness without overpowering the space.

Large rooms or higher ceilings (living rooms, open-plan spaces)

Large areas need more coverage, and higher ceilings benefit from stronger, evenly distributed lighting.

Pro tip: for larger areas, consider multiple light sources or layered lighting, such as combining ceiling lights with downlights or wall sconces, to eliminate shadows and create balanced illumination.

Brightness and lumens: don't just look at watts

In the past we used watts to measure brightness. With LED technology, lumens (the actual light output) are what truly matter. Here is a quick guide to how many lumens you typically need per room:

Room typeSuggested lumen range
Bedrooms1,000 to 2,000 lumens
Kitchens3,000 to 4,000 lumens
Living rooms2,000 to 3,000 lumens
Bathrooms2,000 to 3,000 lumens

All of our ceiling and panel lights provide high lumens and CCT adjustability, giving you the freedom to customise the lighting temperature and intensity to your exact preferences.

Choose the right colour temperature

Colour temperature is measured in Kelvin (K) and affects the mood of a room:

  • Warm white (2700K to 3000K): cosy and relaxing, ideal for bedrooms and living rooms.
  • Cool white (4000K to 5000K): bright and clean, great for kitchens and bathrooms.
  • Daylight (6000K+): crisp and energising, ideal for garages or workspaces.

A CCT-switchable light lets your electrician select one of these settings at installation, so you are not locked into a choice made before the room is painted and furnished.

Energy efficiency, smart features and installation

Greenhse Technologies Perth is committed to eco-friendly, energy-efficient lighting that meets the latest industry standards.

  • Most ceiling and panel lights come with CCT switching, dimmable options and long warranties.
  • We also offer smart LED ceiling lights with WiFi control, timer functions and app integration.

Ease of installation and maintenance matters too. All Greenhse ceiling lights are designed for fast, secure mounting, with clear instructions and compatibility with all types of lighting fittings. Installation must be carried out by a licensed electrician. Most lights last over 30,000 to 50,000 hours, so you won't need to worry about frequent maintenance or failures.

Final thoughts: the right ceiling light makes all the difference

Lighting isn't just functional. It defines how your home looks and feels. Whether you need ceiling lights in Perth, oyster lights for smaller spaces, or panel lights for large open areas, Greenhse Technologies Perth has a range that fits every style, budget and performance need. Visit the No.1 LED lighting store in Perth at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069, or call (08) 9297 2969 for advice on your home.

Why LED lighting for industrial facilities?

LED industrial lighting is built for the toughest environments, including warehouses, mines and agricultural sites. It delivers powerful light, energy savings and durability that traditional lighting cannot match.

Out with the old, in with LEDs

Fluorescent tubes were the standard in industrial buildings for decades, but they are now harder to replace, less energy-efficient and outdated. LEDs have taken over in Perth and across Australia for three big reasons:

  • Energy savings, with lower power bills.
  • Longer lifespans, with fewer entries on the maintenance schedule.
  • Better light quality, for safer, cleaner working environments.

Greenhse Technologies Perth also offers smart LED lighting tailored to Perth's industrial and commercial sites.

Key factors to consider before choosing industrial lighting

Choosing the right LED industrial lighting is not just about picking the brightest product on the shelf. Here is what matters.

1. Light output (lumens, not watts)

Watts measure power consumed, not brightness. For LEDs the figure that counts is lumens, which measures visible light output. Look for enough lumens for the workspace, whether that is a high bay in a warehouse or a focused area on a factory floor.

2. Energy efficiency

LEDs make the most of every watt. Compare fittings by luminous efficacy, measured in lumens per watt, to get both brightness and savings.

3. Durability and environment resistance

Industrial spaces are harsh. Dust, moisture and high temperatures punish old lighting. Choose fixtures rated for the realities of your site, especially IP65-rated or higher where fittings are exposed to the elements.

Quality LEDs can last 10 times longer than fluorescent options, which means fewer climbs up the ladder. Look for a 50 000 Hr rated lifespan for the best quality and value.

5. Colour Rendering Index (CRI)

CRI describes how accurately a light shows colours compared with daylight. To see every bolt and cable clearly, even at night, choose LEDs with a CRI of 80 or higher for superior colour accuracy and visual comfort.

6. Flexibility and controls

Modern industrial lighting is smart. Options with sensors, dimmers and smart controllers let you match light levels to activity and cut energy bills further.

7. Compliance and safety standards

Australian workplaces are highly regulated. Always choose lighting that is certified and compliant with the latest Australian standards for industrial lighting, and have it installed by a licensed electrician.

Lighting plays a more prominent role in your home's appearance and everyday living experience than you might expect. The right lighting enhances comfort, improves functionality and highlights your interior and outdoor design. Yet many Perth homeowners unknowingly make lighting choices that leave their homes feeling dull, uncomfortable or inefficient.

Whether you are building a new home, renovating or replacing outdated fixtures, avoiding the ten common mistakes below will help you create a brighter, more inviting living space.

1. Choosing the wrong colour temperature

A common mistake is selecting lights on brightness alone without considering colour temperature, which has a major effect on the mood and function of each room.

  • Warm White (2700K to 3000K): ideal for living rooms, bedrooms and dining areas where a cosy atmosphere is preferred.
  • Cool White (4000K): great for kitchens, bathrooms, laundries and workspaces where clear visibility matters.
  • Daylight (5000K to 6500K): best suited to garages, workshops and commercial environments that need maximum brightness.

Cool white throughout the whole home feels harsh, while warm light in task areas reduces visibility. Recommended products: LED Downlights, LED bulbs and pendant lights with selectable colour temperatures.

2. Relying on a single light source

Many homes rely on one central ceiling light per room. It provides general light but cannot reach every corner properly. A well-designed plan uses three layers:

  • Ambient lighting for overall illumination.
  • Task lighting for cooking, reading or working.
  • Accent lighting to highlight artwork, shelving or architectural features.

Combining the layers creates a balanced space that is both functional and visually appealing. Recommended products: Ceiling Lights, pendant lights, wall lights, LED Strip Lighting and table lamps.

3. Ignoring Perth's natural sunlight

Perth enjoys more sunshine than most Australian cities, making natural light one of your home's greatest assets. Artificial lighting should complement daylight rather than compete with it:

  • Position lighting to reduce shadows.
  • Install dimmable LED fixtures so brightness can be adjusted through the day.
  • Choose lighting that complements rather than overpowers daylight.

This improves comfort while reducing unnecessary electricity use. Recommended products: dimmable LED downlights, smart lighting systems and LED panels.

4. Using the wrong brightness

Many people still choose lighting by watts instead of lumens. Watts measure energy consumption, while lumens measure actual brightness. As a general guide for the whole room:

  • Living room: 1,500 to 3,000 lumens
  • Kitchen: 3,000 to 4,000 lumens
  • Bedroom: 1,000 to 2,000 lumens
  • Bathroom: 2,000 to 4,000 lumens
  • Home office: 3,000 lumens or more

The right brightness keeps every room comfortable without feeling too dark or overly bright.

5. Overlooking outdoor lighting

Outdoor lighting is not just about appearance. It improves safety, security and usability after sunset. Common mistakes include poorly lit pathways, dark entryways, inadequate driveway lighting, ignoring patios and entertaining areas, and forgetting garden feature lighting. A thoughtful outdoor design makes the property safer and more inviting for family and guests. Recommended products: Outdoor Wall Lights, Garden Lights, bollard lights, flood lights and security lights.

6. Choosing style over function

It is easy to fall in love with a beautiful fixture, but appearance should never come at the expense of practicality. Decorative pendants must provide adequate light over kitchen islands, bathroom fixtures should give clear, even light around mirrors, and home offices need task lighting that reduces eye strain. The best lighting combines attractive design with everyday function.

7. Forgetting about energy efficiency

LED lighting has become the preferred choice for modern Perth homes because it is far more energy-efficient than traditional lighting. Benefits include lower electricity consumption, a longer lifespan than traditional bulbs, reduced maintenance, better light quality and environmentally friendly performance. Upgrading older halogen or incandescent fixtures to LED can significantly reduce household energy costs. Recommended products: LED downlights, LED bulbs, LED panels and smart LED lighting.

8. Right placement of lighting

Even premium products will not perform if they are installed in the wrong location. Common placement mistakes include pendants hung too high or too low, uneven spacing between downlights, shadows on kitchen benchtops, insufficient lighting near mirrors and dark corners in living rooms. Planning fixture placement carefully ensures every area receives the right amount of illumination.

9. Not using smart lighting

Modern lighting is about more than turning lights on and off, and smart lighting products are available at the Greenhse lighting store in Perth. Smart systems let you adjust brightness with dimmers, schedule lighting automatically, control lights remotely from a smartphone, create customised scenes and improve energy efficiency through automation. Recommended products: smart LED bulbs, Smart Switches, motion sensor lights and dimmers.

10. Buying cheap, low-quality fixtures

Budget fixtures may look like a good deal, but they often have shorter lifespans, inconsistent light output and lower build quality. Investing in quality lighting provides better durability, reliable performance, improved safety, superior energy efficiency and lower replacement costs over time. Well-made fixtures are a long-term investment for both your home and your wallet.

When should you upgrade your home lighting?

It may be time for an upgrade if you notice flickering or inconsistent lighting, high electricity bills, outdated halogen or fluorescent fixtures, rooms that feel too dark, poor visibility while cooking or working, or limited lighting control. Replacing outdated fixtures with modern LED solutions instantly improves comfort, aesthetics and energy efficiency.

Final thoughts

Lighting transforms the way your home looks, feels and functions. Avoiding these common mistakes creates spaces that are brighter, more comfortable and more energy-efficient, while adding value to your property. Choosing the right lighting products is as important as choosing furniture or paint colours. From LED downlights and indoor lights to outdoor lighting, smart lighting and energy-efficient LED solutions, quality products deliver lasting performance. /blog/connect-smart-devices-with-smart-l.lede: In today's world, smart home automation transforms how we interact with our devices.
/blog/connect-smart-devices-with-smart-l.bodyHtml:
In today's world, smart home automation transforms how we interact with our devices. The Smart Life App is a powerful tool that allows you to connect and control multiple smart devices from a single platform, making home automation seamless and efficient. This post explains what the app does, walks through the step-by-step process for connecting a new device, and covers the small details that make pairing succeed first time.

Greenhse Technologies in Perth supplies smart downlights, ceiling lights, strip lights, switches and plugs that all pair with the Smart Life App, so once you have learnt the process for one device you can use it for the whole home.

What the Smart Life App does

Smart Life is the free companion app used by a wide range of Wi-Fi and Bluetooth smart products. Instead of having a separate app for every brand of bulb, plug or switch, you add each device to Smart Life and control everything from one screen. Devices can be grouped by room, switched together, dimmed, colour-tuned and scheduled, and the app also links to voice assistants.

The app is available for both iPhone and Android phones. You will need a home Wi-Fi network, your Wi-Fi password and a few minutes for each device.

Step-by-step guide to connecting smart devices

If you're new to smart home technology, watch our instructional video, Connecting Smart Devices using your SmartLife App, for a step-by-step tutorial. It provides a simple and easy-to-follow process, helping you pair your Wi-Fi-enabled smart bulbs, plugs, switches and other IoT devices with the Smart Life App. The written steps below follow the same order as the video.

  1. Install the app and create an account. Download Smart Life from the App Store or Google Play, open it, and register with your email address or phone number. Choose Australia as your region so the app connects to the correct server.
  2. Connect your phone to 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. Most smart lighting devices only communicate on the 2.4GHz band. If your router broadcasts a combined 2.4GHz and 5GHz network, connect your phone to the 2.4GHz network for the duration of the pairing process.
  3. Power the device and put it in pairing mode. Have your electrician install and power up the light or switch first. A new device normally enters pairing mode automatically and the light blinks quickly. If it does not, switch the light off and on three times at the wall switch to reset it, then wait for the fast blink.
  4. Add the device in the app. Tap the plus symbol in the top right corner of the home screen and choose Add Device. The app will scan for nearby devices in pairing mode and list them; for a Bluetooth device, make sure Bluetooth is enabled on your phone.
  5. Enter your Wi-Fi details. Confirm the 2.4GHz network name and type in the password carefully. The app sends these details to the device so it can join your network on its own.
  6. Wait for confirmation and name the device. When the app reports Added successfully, give the device a clear name such as Kitchen Downlights or Bedside Lamp and assign it to a room. In the video you can see two devices, K1 and K2, added in one session.
  7. Test it. Tap the device tile and switch it on and off, dim it, and change colour temperature if the fitting supports it. Then tap Done.

Stand close to the device with the phone for the first pairing. Once the device is on your network you can control it from any distance.

Why use the Smart Life App?

  • Easy setup: a quick and straightforward pairing process, with the same steps for every compatible product.
  • Voice control: compatible with Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, so lights can be switched, dimmed and grouped by voice once the accounts are linked.
  • Remote access: control your devices from anywhere with an internet connection, whether you are at work or on holiday.
  • Automation and scheduling: set timers and routines for smart living, such as outdoor lights that switch on at sunset or bedroom lights that dim gradually at night.

Troubleshooting common pairing problems

  • The device is not found. Check the light is blinking quickly, and that your phone is on the 2.4GHz network with location permission granted to the app.
  • Pairing times out. Re-enter the Wi-Fi password, move closer to the router, and reset the device by switching it off and on three times.
  • Several devices to add. Put all of them into pairing mode together and the app will find and add them in one batch, as shown in the video.
  • Weak signal in part of the house. A Wi-Fi extender or mesh access point will give lights at the far end of the home a stable connection.

Following the video steps, you can effortlessly integrate your smart home devices and enjoy a more convenient lifestyle. Any hard-wired lights and switches must be installed by a licensed electrician; once they are powered, the pairing itself is something any homeowner can do. Following 'What Do You Need To Make Your Home Smart?' and 'Smart Lighting Products and Accessories in Perth', this guide covers connecting smart switches, lights, kinetic switches, Zigbee devices and gateways on the Smart Life or Tuya app.

A. Connecting and set-up

Ensure your WiFi works well. For more than 10 smart devices, invest in a good extender such as the UBIQUITI U6-LR.

  1. Set up a separate 2.4GHz network with its own name and password, or ask your provider or WiFi supplier to. Use a name and password you can enter correctly every time.
  2. Load and register the Smart Life or Tuya app. With products at home and at the office, register both apps, one for each, with Alexa or Google on a different account for each. This keeps management simpler.
  3. Select the 2.4GHz option on your smart device and check signal strength where it will be added (3 bars or more).
  4. Follow the product instructions using the same 2.4GHz name and password.

Note: Band Steering on some routers prioritises 5GHz and switches to 2.4GHz further from the router, but both bands then share one name and password. Turn it off to set separate names.

Tip: home routers often handle a maximum of 12 devices per band; beyond that, devices disconnect. An extender allows 300 or more with better range and management. Connect it by data cable (recommended), reuse the same 2.4GHz and 5GHz names and passwords, turn off the router WiFi, and devices will not need resetting.

B. Connecting lights

  1. Ensure you are on the 2.4GHz network.
  2. Devices can be added by Add Manually or Auto Scan; we recommend Add Manually.
  3. Select the light to pair. Enter pairing mode: turn it ON, OFF after 10 seconds, then ON.
  4. Next turn ON-OFF-ON-OFF-ON, keeping each interval short and turning OFF only after the light is ON.
  5. Confirm it flashes rapidly (four times per second).
  6. Add the device with the light ON. It then appears on your Home page.

C. Connecting smart switches

  1. Complete section A once the switch is wired and covered. Fit it straight with no side gaps, on a smooth surface, screws not over tightened: the sensor is light sensitive and any gap or uneven fit causes poor operation. Turn on main power only after installation with the crystal glass cover fitted. Opening tabs facing away from a door lintel or wall end ease later removal.
  2. Wait 10 seconds after the switch lights come on. On 1, 2, 3 or 4 gangs all indicators are green.
  3. Touch one switch (no pressure needed); it turns red.
  4. Touch and hold about 7 seconds. A slight click sounds and the WiFi indicator flashes blue quickly, ready to link.
  5. In the app select Electrical in the left-hand menu, then Switch WiFi, and follow the instructions.
  6. Rename the switch (Kitchen, Dining), then each individual switch (Downlights, Pendant, Strip Light).
  7. Once all switches are connected and named, pair any needed as 2-way or 3-way or linked to remotes or smart plugs: select the first switch, tap the top right Edit button, scroll down to Multi-control association.
  8. Select the individual switch to pair, push + Link with Switch, select the switch and individual switch to link, and save.

D. Pairing kinetic switches to receiver modules

  1. With the receiver module wired, push the square linking button until the red light flashes slowly. Release, then push the kinetic switch once quickly. Push the correct switch, as unlinking is harder.
  2. To unlink, hold the square button about 12 seconds: the red light flashes slowly, then quickly, then stops. Release and the switch is unlinked.
  3. A dual receiver module drives 2 devices from different switches. Link the first as above: push 3 seconds until red flashes, release, push the first kinetic switch once quickly. For the second, push the square button twice quickly so the light turns blue, hold 3 seconds until blue flashes, then push the second kinetic switch once to pair it to the second output. Push the square button twice quickly to return to red.
  4. Multiple switches can link to one receiver and multiple receivers to one switch, so plan carefully or incorrect switching and unlinking will follow. A dual controller may need both red and blue channels unlinked.
  5. SMART receivers must join the home WiFi as in section A. When turned ON the red light flashes quickly. Open the app and push + to add a device.
  6. The receiver module appears; select Add device, then rename it.
  7. For a Smart Dimmer module, set the minimum level so light is visible with no flicker. Greenhse downlights dim 0 to 100% without flickering; other brands may not.
  8. Link a smart receiver to a kinetic switch: push + Pair, then push the kinetic switch once.
  9. With smart receivers on WiFi and linked to kinetic switches, many options open up under Scene at the bottom of the app.

E. Connecting Zigbee devices

  1. Add the Zigbee gateway first. Push RESET until the indicator flashes.
  2. Select Gateway Control on the Select Device Type menu, then Gateway (Zigbee), the 2nd option. The gateway's green light must stay on. Follow the app.
  3. The gateway then appears on the Home page.
  4. To add a Zigbee device, open Home, tap + in the upper right corner and find the device.
  5. Select the gateway, which should be no more than 5m from the Zigbee devices. Reset the device to pairing mode (indicator flashing) and add it.
  6. The Zigbee device then appears on the Home page.

F. Connecting a Bluetooth gateway

  1. Locate the wireless gateway (Bluetooth) under Gateway Control, as in E1.
  2. Power the gateway ON and turn on the phone's Bluetooth.
  3. Hold the gateway reset button for 5 seconds until one indicator flashes fast (red flashing, blue always on).
  4. Once added, open the gateway, select + Add Device, and add all devices together.

Fixed wiring must be done by a licensed electrician. For help, call Greenhse Technologies in Perth on (08) 9297 2969 or visit 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069.
/blog/connecting-and-set-up-of-smart-swi.bodyHtmlOriginal:
After reading the previous blogs, 'What Do You Need To Make Your Home Smart?' and 'Smart Lighting Products and Accessories in Perth', this blog will help you with connecting and setting up Smart Switches on the “Smart Life” or “Tuya” App.

A. CONNECTING AND SET-UP:

Ensure your WiFi is set up and working well, and if you plan on using more than 10 Smart devices, invest in a good WiFi extender, such as the UBIQUITI U6-LR.

  1. Set up a separate 2.4GHz network with its own name and password, or ask your provider/WiFi supplier to set this up before leaving. Please use a name and password you can remember correctly and get right each time.
  2. Load and register the “Smart Life” or “Tuya” App. (Note; if you are using products at your home and your office, register both apps and use one for each. This will make managing devices a lot simpler. Also, register Alexa or Google to a different account for each.)

  3. Select the 2.4GHz WiFi option on your Smart device and ensure you have good connection strength where the device will be added. (3 bars or more on signal strength).
  4. Follow the product installation instructions and use the same 2.4GHz name and password.

NOTE: Some Wifi Routers will have a function called “Band Steering” This can be useful for     5GHz products, as it will prioritise 5GHz but when moving further from the router will switch to 2.5GHz to maintain a connection. The problem with Band Steering is that both the 2.4GHz and 5GHz will have the same name and password. In order to set up different names, this will need to be turned off.

TIP: Standard Home Routers are not designed to handle many devices, often 12 is the maximum on each band. If you exceed the number of devices, you will find these disconnecting on your phone. WiFi Extenders can increase the number of devices up to 300 or more and offer better and quicker WiFi management and range.

If you add a WiFi extender, using a data cable link, (recommended) and use the same name and password on the 2.4GHz and 5GHz extender networks, turn off the router WiFi and your devices will not need to be reset.

 

B. CONNECTING LIGHTS

  1. Ensure that you are on the 2.4GHz network.
  2. There are 2 ways to add devices: ‘ADD MANUALLY’ or ‘AUTO SCAN’
  3. We recommend ‘MANUALLY’  adding devices by:
    1. Select the light that you want to pair with the App. Make sure that the light is in PAIRING mode by turning ON the device then turn it OFF after 10sec then turn it back ON.
    2. Next Turn ON-OFF-ON-OFF-ON (Keep the time interval short. Turn OFF after the light is ON
    3. Confirm that the light is rapidly flashing (four times per second)
    4. Add device - ensure that the device is ON. Once it is successfully added the Smart device will now be added to your Home page.

 

C. CONNECTING SMART SWITCHES

  1. Follow “A” once a switch has been connected and a cover placed on the switch. (Ensure the switch has been fitted straight with no gaps on the side, that the surface is smooth, and that screws are not over tightened as the sensor is light sensitive. Any gaps, or uneven fitting, will cause poor functioning.) Turn on the main power ONLY after installation and with Crystal glass cover fitted. (Note: placing a switch with opening tabs facing away from a door lintel or end of the wall will allow easier removal later).
  2. Wait 10 seconds after the switch lights turn on. For 1,2, 3 or 4 Gangs, all indicators will be green.
  3. Touch one of the switches. (Note: No pressure is required, switches are light sensitive) The switch will turn red.
  4. Touch and hold this switch for about 7 seconds. You will hear a slight click, and the wifi indicator light will flash blue quickly.
  5. The flashing indicator shows the switch is ready to be linked to the WiFi. On the App, select “electrical” on the left-hand side menu, select “Switch WiFi,” and follow the instructions to connect to your WiFi.
  6. Rename the switch, i.e. Kitchen, Dining, then rename each individual switch i.e. Downlights, pendant, strip light, etc. This is important for a number of reasons.
  7. Once all switches have been connected to the WiFi and named, you can then select the switches that need to be paired as 2- or 3-way or even connected to remote controllers or Smart plugs. To link 2 or more switches together, select the first switch you want to link, then select the top right-hand “edit” button, scroll down and select ”Multi-control association.”
  8. Select the first individual switch you want to pair, then push “+ Link with Switch.” Select the switch and then the individual switch to link and save.

 

D. PAIRING KINETIC SWITCHES TO RECEIVER MODULES:

  1. Once the receiver Module has been wired, push the square linking button until the red light flashes slowly. Release, then push the Kinetic switch that is being linked to it once quickly and let go. (Be careful not to push the incorrect switch as un-linking is more difficult.)
  2. To unlink, the switch needs to be pushed for about 12 seconds. The red light will flash slowly, and then it will flash quickly, then it will stop flashing. Stop pushing the square button and the switch will be unlinked.
  3. A dual receiver Module can connect to 2 separate devices with different switches. Connecting the first device to the first switch is the same as all receivers. Push for 3 seconds until red light flashes, let go and push the Kinetic switch once quickly and let go. To connect the second device, quickly push the square button twice, and the light will turn blue. Push and hold the square button for 3 seconds and blue light will flash. Push the second Kinetic switch once quickly to pair the second switch to the second output on the receiver Module to get back to the red light. Push the square button twice quickly to get back to the red light.
  4. Note multiple switches can be linked to a single receiver, and multiple receivers can be linked to one switch; carefully plan and link correctly, or incorrect switching will occur, and unlinking will be required. The dual controller may need to unlink both red and blue channels.
  5. SMART receivers must be linked to the home WiFi as in “A” above.
  6. When the Smart Receiver Module is turned ON, the Red light will flash quickly. Open the App and push “+” to add a device.
  7. The receiver Module will open on the App; select ‘Add device.’ Once the device (Receiver Module) is added, select and change the name. 
  8. If the “Smart Dimmer” module has been added, set the “minimum level” to ensure light can be seen and no flickering. (Note: With Greenhse downlights dimming can be 0-100% with no flickering; other brands may not all have this quality or option). 
  9. After Smart receivers have been added they can be linked to a Kinetic switch by pushing the "+ Pair" button, then pushing the Kinetic switch you want to link to it , once.
  10. With the Smart receivers linked to the WiFi and Kinetic switches, numerous options are available using the "Scene" function on the bottom of the App page.

 

E. CONNECTING ZIGBEE DEVICES

  1. First, add the Zigbee Gateway. Push the RESET button until the indicator light flashes.
  2. Select ‘Gateway Control’ on the ‘Select Device Type’ menu, then select ‘Gateway (Zigbee)’ which is the 2nd option. Ensure that the Green Light of the Gateway is always on. Follow App instructions.
  3. Once the Gateway has been successfully added, you can find the Zigbee Gateway in the Home Page.
  4. To Add a Zigbee Device - Open the App ‘Home’, click the ‘+’ button in the upper right-hand corner and find the device (Zigbee) that needs to be added.
  5. Select the Zigbee Gateway that you want to connect. The Zigbee Gateway should be no more than 5m away from the Zigbee Devices. Follow the instructions on the App. Reset the Zigbee device to pairing mode (the indicator light should be flashing) and add the device.
  6. After the addition is successful you can find the Zigbee device on the Home page.

 

F. CONNECTING BLUETOOTH GATEWAY

  1. Locate the wireless gateway (Bluetooth) under "Gateway Control” as in E 1 above
  2. Make sure the Gateway is powered ON and turn ON the Bluetooth switch of the phone
  3. Press and hold the reset button of the Bluetooth gateway for 5 seconds until one of the two indicator lights enters a fast flashing state (red light flashes, blue light is always on)
  4. Once the Gateway has been added, select and open the Bluetooth Gateway and select ‘+ Add Device’. All devices can be added together.

Are you looking for a straightforward way to control your smart devices simultaneously? The SMART Life app makes it easy. This guide explains what a Group is, how to create one step by step, which devices can be grouped together, and a few limits worth knowing before you start. It follows the same process shown in our video, How to Create "Groups" with SMART Life App.

If you create a group of smart lights, you can turn all the lights on or off and change the brightness or colour temperature of every light at the same time, from a single control panel, instead of opening each light one by one.

What is a Group in the SMART Life app?

A Group is a virtual device that combines several real devices of the same type into one tile on your home screen. When you tap the group, the app shows one control panel, and every command you send is applied to all members of the group at once.

This is different from a Room, which is only a way of sorting devices into a list, and different from a Scene or Automation, which runs a saved set of actions. A group behaves like one large device: one on and off switch, one brightness slider, one colour temperature slider, one colour wheel.

Typical uses in a Perth home include:

  • Six smart downlights in an open-plan living area treated as one light.
  • All the LED strip lights in a kitchen kickboard run controlled together.
  • A row of garden lights switched on together at dusk.
  • Several smart plugs for a home theatre powered down with one tap.

Before you start

Each device must already be added to the SMART Life app and working on its own. If a light is not yet connected, add it first through the plus icon on the home screen, then come back to grouping. Make sure every device you want to group is online, on the same account, and ideally in the same home within the app.

How to create a group step by step

  1. Open the SMART Life app and go to the Home tab.
  2. Tap one of the devices you want to include in the group. Its control panel opens.
  3. Tap the edit icon (a pencil) in the top right corner of the control panel. The device settings screen appears.
  4. Tap Create Group.
  5. The app lists every compatible device of the same type. Tick each device you want to include. The device you started from is already selected.
  6. Tap Save.
  7. Give the group a clear name, for example Living Room Lights or Alfresco, then tap Save again.
  8. Return to the Home tab. The new group appears as its own tile. Tap it to open the shared control panel.

To edit a group later, open the group, tap the edit icon, and choose Edit Group to add or remove devices, rename it, or dismiss the group entirely. Dismissing a group removes only the group; the individual devices stay in the app.

Controlling a group

The group control panel shows the same features as the devices inside it. For a group of colour temperature downlights you can:

  • Switch all lights on or off together.
  • Drag the brightness slider to dim every light to the same level.
  • Move the colour temperature slider between warm white and cool white for the whole group.
  • Use the group in a Scene or Automation, so a single tap or a sunset trigger adjusts all lights at once.
  • Ask Google Assistant or Amazon Alexa to control the group by name, once the app is linked to your voice assistant.

You can still open any single device inside the group and adjust it on its own. The next group command simply brings it back in line with the others.

What can be grouped and what the limits are

Groups only work across devices of the same category and, in most cases, the same product type. A few practical rules:

  • Lights can be grouped with lights that share the same capabilities. A group of CCT downlights works well; mixing a single-colour light with an RGB light usually means the group only offers the features they share, or the app will not list them together.
  • Wi-Fi devices group with Wi-Fi devices, and Bluetooth mesh or Zigbee devices group with devices of the same protocol under the same gateway.
  • Smart plugs and switches group with other plugs and switches.
  • Different product families, such as a light and a fan, cannot be placed in one group. Use a Scene to control mixed devices together.
  • Each device can belong to more than one group, so a downlight can sit in both a Kitchen group and a Whole Downstairs group.
  • Keep groups to a sensible size. Very large groups of Wi-Fi devices can respond a little slower because each device receives its own command over your network.

If the Create Group option does not appear, the device model does not support grouping, or there is no second compatible device on the account yet.

Tips for a tidy setup

  • Name groups by location and purpose so voice commands are easy to remember.
  • Keep the Wi-Fi signal strong throughout the house so grouped devices respond together. A mesh Wi-Fi system helps in larger homes.
  • After creating a group, test it once with lights on, once with lights off, and once with a brightness change to confirm every device responds.

Grouping is one of the quickest ways to make a smart lighting setup feel effortless, and it costs nothing more than a few minutes in the app. Order today the Smart LED lighting products in Perth from Greenhse Technologies, or visit our showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069. Call (08) 9297 2969 if you would like help choosing SMART Life compatible lights or setting up groups, scenes and automations for your home.

/blog/everything-you-need-to-know-about-.bodyHtml:
Strip lighting can create the most attractive lighting in a home or commercial property if it is done correctly. There are so many different styles, outputs and colours that selection can be difficult. This article covers everything you need to know about strip lighting: brightness, LEDs per metre, colour, IP rating, controllers, aluminium channels and run lengths, so you can choose the right strip for kitchens, bathrooms, joinery and feature areas.

Brightness

Strip lights can produce anywhere between 100 lumens per metre and 3000 lumens per metre on a single row of strip. For comparison, a light bulb or downlight produces close to 1000 lumens. If you are using strip light to light up a kitchen bench, bathroom basin or make-up area, high lumens are very important because the strip is doing task lighting. For decorative areas such as under a floating vanity, along a bulkhead or behind a TV, lower lumens are more suitable and more comfortable.

LEDs per metre and the dot effect

Higher lumen strip normally has more LEDs per metre, typically 190 to 240, which gives bright and even distribution up to 3000 lumens per metre. Many lower output strips have LEDs spaced out at 30 to 60 LEDs per metre, which look uneven and unattractive, especially through a diffuser, because you can see each individual point of light. This is known as the dot effect.

A new COB strip light is the best solution for lower lumen applications. COB (chip on board) strip is a continuous line of light with no dots, which is very attractive, yet it still delivers 1200 lumens per metre with lower power requirements.

Pictured: 24V COB 4000K IP65 strip.

Colour

Colour can change the complete appearance of a space. Not only full colour RGB (red, green, blue), but even the white selection, from 2700K warm white to 6400K cool white, makes a big difference. Warm white feels cosy and suits living areas and bedrooms, natural white suits kitchens and bathrooms, and cool white suits workshops and commercial fit-outs.

Strip light is available in single colour, in warm, natural or bright white, as well as CCT adjustable, which lets you select your exact colour temperature and brightness from a remote or app. CCT adjustable strip is also available in COB, which is dotless and very attractive.

Pictured: 24V COB single colours in warm, natural and bright white.

IP rating

If strip light is being used in wet areas or places with high moisture content, IP65 is required. A silicon gel coating covers and protects the LED chips and connections. Even in dry areas the silicon gel is useful for adding extra strength and protection against knocks and dust.

Note: when choosing single colour strip light, ensure the output colour is correct, because the gel coating changes the LED colour. A 3000K LED with gel coating gives a cooler 3800K appearance, so confirm the finished colour rather than the bare chip colour.

For outdoors, IP65 can work, but with time and erosive elements including UV and rain the strip light will not last. A silicon sleeve with gel injected inside gives a much more durable product with an IP68 rating, and is the right choice for exposed outdoor runs.

Controllers

Various controllers are available and the strip type decides what you need.

  • Single colour strips do not need a controller. However, a dimming module is useful for setting the brightness level and turning the strip on and off with a remote or smart device, including Google and Alexa.
  • CCT strips require a controller for setting the colour temperature and brightness level.
  • RGB strips require a controller for setting the colour selection and brightness.

Controllers work with hand or wall remotes and also provide options for smart phones and voice activation through Google or Alexa. Controllers can be linked wirelessly to switches, sensors or cameras, adding convenient automation options such as a kickboard strip that comes on when the kitchen sensor detects movement at night.

Channel

Aluminium channels are often required to complete an installation. They hold the strip straight, draw heat away from the LEDs and give a finished, professional look. Recess wing channels are normally recessed into cabinetry, while rectangular and thin channels can be added as a retrofit if recesses cannot be made. Channels are usually available in silver aluminium, but black and white profiles are now also available in some styles. The channels have 15% to 20% diffusers, which hide the strip and help diffuse the light further.

Length

24-volt strip lights are available in lengths up to 10 metres and can be cut in increments of 5cm. When placing a strip, make sure the cut end is flush with the end of the channel or application. The wired end can be bent into a 12mm hole at the end, ensuring the strip reaches end to end with no gap in the light.

Up to 2 x 10 metre lengths can be run from 1 controller, increasing the total length to 20 metres. By adding transformers, longer runs can be achieved. Size the transformer to the strip wattage per metre multiplied by the total length, with some spare capacity.

12-volt strip lighting runs a lot hotter than 24-volt strip and is limited to 5 metre lengths before the far end noticeably dims. Due to the extra heat, 12V strip also tends to have a much shorter lifespan, which is why 24V is the standard for quality installations.

To see the product in action, watch the video GH 24V COB Professional Strip Lighting on our website.

Choosing the right lumens, colour, IP rating, controller and channel up front is what separates a stunning strip light installation from a disappointing one. Visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 or call (08) 9297 2969 to plan your strip lighting project.

/blog/garden-light-connection-guide-sing.lede: Greenhse Technologies offers high-quality, energy-efficient LED Garden Lights in Perth that help make your garden brighter and more appealing.
/blog/garden-light-connection-guide-sing.bodyHtml:
Greenhse Technologies offers high-quality, energy-efficient LED garden lights in Perth that help make your garden brighter and more appealing. They enhance the look of your outdoor spaces while reducing energy consumption, and they come in a range of colour options, including RGB, Natural White and Warm White, to suit your garden's style and mood.

Connecting LED garden lights involves several key components and steps that must be followed carefully. This guide walks through the single colour connection diagram: the transformer, the controller, the cable and the lights, plus the three layouts you can choose from. Review the specifications below before ordering so that every part is compatible and the system performs reliably for years.

Why garden lighting is worth doing well

Well-placed garden lights transform a home's exterior after dark. Whether you are illuminating pathways, highlighting garden features or creating a relaxing space for evening gatherings, LED garden lights give you the versatility and brightness you need, all year round. Because the system runs on 12V direct current from a plug-in transformer, the outdoor cabling is extra-low voltage. The 240V side of the transformer must still be installed by a licensed electrician if a new outdoor power point is required.

Components in the single colour system

  • 10W LED garden light with 1 m of cable attached, available in 3000K (Warm White) or 4000K (Natural White), $28 +GST each. See the 10W LED Garden Light.
  • 200W 12V (IP65) transformer, suitable for up to 16 lights, $110 +GST.
  • 75W 12V IP65 transformer, suitable for up to 7 lights, $75 +GST.
  • 2-core rubberised cable for the run between the lights, $2 +GST per metre.
  • 2-in-1 controller (single colour or dual white), $15 +GST, which adds dimming and control. See the Single Colour/Dual White LED Controller.
  • 2-in-1 SMART controller, $25 +GST, which adds app control through the TUYA or SMART Life app on a smart device or mobile phone, including timers, schedules and other SMART functions.
  • Black or white Sunrise remote, CCT adjustable and dimming, $18 +GST.
  • Black or white 4-zone glass remote, $35 +GST.

Sizing is simple: each light draws 10W, so the 75W transformer comfortably runs 7 lights and the 200W transformer runs 16. Do not exceed these counts, because an overloaded transformer runs hot and fails early.

Wiring the 2-in-1 controller

The controller sits between the transformer and the lights. Its terminals are marked and the polarity matters.

  • Input: V+ to the red wire and V- to the black wire from the transformer.
  • Output: red to V+ and black to V- on the light cable.
  • If the controller is wired incorrectly it will fail, and this is not covered by warranty. Check red and black twice before switching on.
  • After power is applied, the SET button must be selected so that the RED light shows on the controller. This confirms the controller is in the correct mode and ready to pair with a remote or the app.

Three connection layouts

Layout 1: no controller, up to 16 lights

  1. Plug the 200W 12V (IP65) transformer into the outdoor power point.
  2. Run 2-core rubberised cable from the transformer output along the garden bed. This run can be any length.
  3. Join each garden light's 1 m lead to the main cable, matching red to red and black to black.
  4. Connect up to 16 lights. The lights switch on and off with the transformer, so use a switched power point or a timer.

Layout 2: two controllers, up to 16 lights

  1. Plug in the 200W 12V (IP65) transformer.
  2. Connect two 2-in-1 controllers to the transformer output, each wired V+ red and V- black as described above.
  3. From each controller, run about 1 m of cable to the start of its own light run.
  4. Connect up to 8 lights on each controller, giving up to 16 lights in total, with two independently dimmable zones.

Layout 3: optional controller, up to 7 lights

  1. Plug in the 75W 12V IP65 transformer.
  2. Connect one optional 2-in-1 controller or 2-in-1 SMART controller to the transformer output, then run 1 m of cable to the light run.
  3. Connect up to 7 lights. The controller adds dimming and control from a remote or the app.

Choosing a remote or the app

Both 2-in-1 controllers pair with the Sunrise remote for CCT adjustment and dimming, or with the 4-zone glass wall remote for separate zones. The SMART controller also connects to the TUYA or SMART Life app, so you can set sunset timers and schedules, dim the garden from the couch and add the lights to scenes with your indoor smart lighting.

The full diagram is available as a PDF: Single Colour Garden Lights connection guide.

Installation tips

  • Use waterproof joiners on every cable connection and keep joins above ground where possible.
  • Keep polarity consistent along the whole run so every light receives the correct supply.
  • Place the transformer in a sheltered spot even though it is IP65 rated.
  • Leave some spare capacity on the transformer if you plan to add lights later.

Order the correct transformer, controller, cable and lights together and the installation will be straightforward. Greenhse Technologies in Perth can put together a complete garden lighting kit for your layout. Visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 or call (08) 9297 2969 for advice on the right components for your garden.

/blog/guide-connecting-led-rgbw-garden-l.bodyHtml:
LED RGBW garden lights provide high-quality, energy-efficient and bright illumination for outdoor areas, and are available exclusively at Greenhse Technologies in Perth. The range includes RGB full colour, Natural White and Warm White varieties, so you can select the right light for each part of the garden. With long-lasting performance and low energy consumption, they are a sustainable and cost-effective choice for landscaping and a home's outdoor lighting, creating a welcoming atmosphere after dark.

This guide explains how a full colour garden lighting system goes together: the LED Garden RGBW lights themselves, the RGB/RGBW/RGBWW LED Controller, the LED wireless remote controllers, the transformer, the cables and connectors, and how to wire them correctly. Getting voltage compatibility and wiring right is what gives the system reliable, long-lasting performance. It is not as complicated as it looks, provided the steps below are followed carefully.

How a 12V RGB garden light system works

The garden lights run on 12 volts, not mains power. A 12V transformer (also called a driver or power supply) plugs into a standard outdoor power point and converts 240V mains to safe low voltage. The transformer feeds a 3-in-1 LED controller, which receives commands from a remote or the Tuya or Smart Life app and sends the colour signal down the cable to the lights. Each light has a 1m cable and connects to the run through a T-piece, so lights daisy-chain along a single line with extension cords between them.

Choosing the transformer and controller

The transformer size depends on how many lights you run. The connection diagram shows two standard configurations:

  • 75W 12V IP65 transformer, $75 + GST: suitable for up to 7 lights, wired through one 3-in-1 LED controller.
  • 200W 12V IP65 transformer, $110 + GST: suitable for up to 16 lights. The transformer feeds two 3-in-1 controllers, each running its own line of up to 8 lights.

Each 3-in-1 controller drives a maximum of 8 lights, so larger gardens use several controllers in parallel from the one transformer. Both controllers can be paired to the same remote or app so all the lights change colour together. IP65 means the transformer is protected against dust and water jets, but it should still be mounted in a sheltered position off the ground.

Controller options are:

  • 3-in-1 Controller, $15 + GST: works with the 2.4GHz wireless remotes.
  • 3-in-1 SMART Controller, $25 + GST: works with the remotes and also with the Tuya or Smart Life app on a smartphone or smart device, allowing timers, schedules and other smart functions.

Wiring the 3-in-1 controller

The controller has an input side from the transformer and an output side to the lights. Polarity matters.

  1. Input: connect V+ to the red wire and V- to the black wire from the transformer. If the input is wired incorrectly the controller will fail, and this is not covered by warranty, so double check before powering up.
  2. Output: connect Black to V+, Red to R, Green to G and Blue to B on the light cable.
  3. SET button: the controller has a SET selector. It must be set so that the RED indicator light shows on the controller. This puts the controller in the correct mode for the RGB garden lights.
  4. Run 1m of cable from the controller to the first T-piece, then continue the line with T-pieces and extension cords.

Fitting the transformer to the power point and any fixed wiring is work for a licensed electrician. The low-voltage plug-and-play cables and T-pieces on the 12V side are designed to be clicked together without tools.

Cables, T-pieces and spacing

Each T-piece has 0.2m tails either side and provides a socket for one light. Extension cords of 1m or 3m run between T-pieces, so you can space lights to suit the garden beds. Prices from the diagram:

  • Garden light with 1m cable, RGB: $38 + GST
  • T-piece: $7 + GST
  • Extension cord 1m: $7 + GST
  • Extension cord 3m: $11 + GST

Count the lights, sketch the run and note the distance between each fitting before ordering. You need one T-piece per light and one extension cord for each gap between T-pieces. To ensure long life, apply silicone to the connectors when joining them. Connectors age over time and water can damage cables and connections, so seal every join and keep plugs above soil level where possible.

Remote and app control

Both controller types are controlled by 2.4GHz wireless remotes:

  • RGB+CCT hand remote, $17 + GST: colour wheel, brightness and white adjustment.
  • Black or White 4-Zone wall remote, RGB+CCT, $35 + GST: a wall-mounted panel that controls up to four separate zones, for example front garden, rear garden, pool area and entry.

With the SMART controller you can also use the Tuya or Smart Life app on a mobile phone to add timers and schedules, set scenes and link the garden lights to voice assistants and the rest of your smart home.

You can also download the complete RGB garden lights connection guide as a PDF to keep on site during installation.

Installation checklist

  1. Decide the number of lights and choose the 75W (up to 7 lights) or 200W (up to 16 lights) 12V transformer.
  2. Choose one 3-in-1 controller per line of up to 8 lights, standard or SMART.
  3. Measure the run and order T-pieces and 1m or 3m extension cords.
  4. Wire the controller input (V+ red, V- black) and output (Black V+, Red R, Green G, Blue B), and set SET to show the RED light.
  5. Seal all connectors with silicone, power up and pair the remote or app.

If you would like help choosing the right components for your garden, Greenhse Technologies in Perth can put a complete kit together for you. Call (08) 9297 2969 or visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 to see the RGBW garden lights in action.
