/blog/popular-smart-lighting-products-pe.lede: Smart Lighting: The most useful Smart product for a home, in my opinion, would be lighting.
/blog/popular-smart-lighting-products-pe.bodyHtml:
Smart lighting: the most useful smart product for a home, in my opinion, would be lighting. Here are the popular smart lighting products and accessories Greenhse Technologies supplies in Perth.

Smart lighting

Smart lights have many advantages:

  • Lights switch by voice or app, or on a schedule.
  • Brightness is selectable from 1 to 100%, giving practical light levels and energy savings when dimmed.
  • Colour temperature adjusts from very warm 2700k to 6500k cool white. Human-centric settings shift it through the day, helping sleep patterns and health.
  • Full-colour options offer blue light for home theatres and colour changing with music for functions or teenagers.

Smart switches

  • App-controlled lights fail if the wall switch is turned off. Smart switches work with normal and smart lighting, with schedules and control from anywhere in the world.
  • Smart switches save construction costs because complicated communication wiring no longer needs planning during a build. They link in many combinations as 2-way, 3-way or more.
  • They can be added with no load wires as 2-way or 3-way switches, and connect to remote smart receivers, strip lighting, garden lights, or smart plugs feeding table lamps and even the Christmas tree.
  • Multiple timers and schedules make any connected item smart.
  • Motion sensors, IP cameras, contact sensors, temperature sensors and more can link to a smart switch, so a visitor at your smart doorbell camera turns on porch, garden and even an inside table light.
  • When you leave, all switches can turn off automatically, leaving one or two lights on if required; on arrival, specific lights switch on at the required level (if smart).

Smart WiFi sockets

  • Two smart WIFI sockets fit side by side on a double GPO, and smart modules can be built into a GPO during construction.
  • Smart plugs switch by app or linked smart switch, with multiple timers and schedules, or by IP cameras, PIR sensors, contact sensors, smoke alarms and more.
  • With 2.5 Amps and optional relay switches, hot water systems, aircon, heat pumps, pool pumps, bore pumps and many other devices can be controlled.
  • Running them in daytime on no-cost solar electricity brings very large energy savings.

Remote or in-ceiling smart modules

  • Any standard lighting system with single wired switches can be converted to smart.
  • Most older homes have single wired switches with no neutral, so stable smart switches (which need a neutral feed) cannot be used; the module goes in the ceiling or at the device, where neutrals exist.
  • Modules give remote switching, dimming and scheduling, and wireless kinetic switches can be linked to them wherever needed.

Smart kinetic switch

  • Smart kinetic switches require no connected wires or even batteries; pressing the switch generates the signal.
  • They connect directly to modules or smart modules near the light or device controlled.
  • Available in 1, 2 and 3 gangs, they are attractive, strong, neat and completely waterproof to IP67.
  • Compatible modules: 1000W receiver, dual 1200W receiver (600W x 2), dimmer 100W receiver, smart 600W receiver and smart dimmer 100W receiver. Depending on the receiver they switch, dim or give smart control.
  • With no wiring, huge construction savings are possible and switches go wherever required.
  • 2-way and 3-way switching works well; multiple switches can link to one receiver, perfect for bedside tables and island benches.
  • Suitable for outdoor areas, wheelchairs and special requirements.

Zigbee smart devices

Zigbee uses the lowest power of WiFi, Bluetooth and Zigbee, so devices run up to 2 years on a small button battery, making installation easy and flexible.

A Zigbee Gateway must be installed first as the bridge between your WiFi and Zigbee devices. Connect it to the router with a data cable, add it in the app on the 2.4GHz network, select the Gateway, press Add device, put each device in pairing mode as indicated, and add it.

  • Contact sensors: very small, for doors, windows or any opening, as security or to activate lights and other smart products.
  • PIR sensors: placed inconspicuously in rooms, hallways and areas needing automated lighting; two or more can switch the same lights for reliability.
  • Temperature sensors: send warnings and switch on fans or other devices. In a fridge, a warning is sent if the temperature exceeds 6º; in rooms they set air conditioning levels; in a fish tank they monitor water remotely.
  • Smoke alarms: emit loud warnings, message your phone and can turn off devices. They do not replace the standard home smoke alarm but suit ancillary areas such as garages and sheds.
  • Water sensors: any over-level or spillage activates alarms and messages.

WiFi cameras, garage door, sensor and water products

WiFi cameras and doorbells need only USB power, or mini solar panels and batteries outdoors. They record visitors to the app message centre, notify your phone and can trigger lights or an alarm, with 2-way voice; some have human detection and adjustable sensor areas so only required alerts arrive. Doorbell cameras have linked indoor chimes that also ring on your mobile, and can turn on front wall, porch or garden lights on motion.

WiFi garage door opener: this WiFi Garage Door Controller notifies you if the door is left open by mistake or has hit an obstruction and reopened. The door can be opened and closed remotely, and it combines with a WiFi camera for peace of mind.

WiFi sensor and sensor light: a WiFi sensor adjusts settings on a smart device, and combined with lights also controls brightness and colour temperature. It gives up to 19 metres range and 90º coverage and connects to other smart devices with no extra wiring (only live and neutral feeds required). Paired with a smart switch or plug it adds switching, scheduling and notifications.

WiFi water switches set correct watering days and times, with a soil and temperature sensor adjusting the schedule for ideal watering without waste.

Hard-wired switches, modules and sockets must be installed by a licensed electrician. To see these smart lighting products in action, visit Greenhse Technologies in Perth at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 or call (08) 9297 2969.

  • Multiple timers and schedules can be set.
  • They can be turned on or off by Smart products such as a Smart Switch, IP Cameras, PIR sensors, contact sensors, smoke alarms and more.
  • With 2.5 Amps and optional relay switches, hot water systems, aircon, heat pumps, pool pumps, bore pumps and numerous devices can be controlled.
  • When set to function during day-time hours while Solar production provides no-cost electricity, this can lead to very large energy cost savings.

 

Remote or In-Ceiling Smart Modules:

  • Any standard lighting system with single wired switches can be converted to Smart.
  • Most old homes have single wired switches with no neutral wires. This prevents stable Smart switches from being used, which require a neutral feed. The remote devices get connected to the ceiling or at the device source where neutral wires exist.
  • Smart modules will enable remote switching, dimming and scheduling.
  • They can also have wireless Kinetic switches linked to them and placed conveniently where required.

 

SMART Kinetic Switch:

  • Smart Kinetic switches require no connected wires or even batteries.
  • Kinetic Switches require no connected wires or even batteries.
  • They connect directly to Modules or Smart Modules placed near the lights or device to be controlled.
  • Available in 1, 2 & 3 gangs; they are attractive, strong, neat, and completely waterproof, IP67.
  • These switches can connect to various different control modules; 
    1. 1000W Receiver
    2. Dual 1200W Receiver (600W x 2)
    3. Dimmer 100W Receiver
    4. Smart 600W Receiver
    5. Smart Dimmer 100W Receiver
  • Depending on the receiver Module selected, Kinetic switches can turn devices on and off, do dimming and even Smart control. 
  • With no wiring required, huge construction cost savings are possible, but more importantly, you have complete flexibility and no limitations. Switches can be added as and where required. 
  • 2-way and 3-way switching works well with this system. Multiple switches can link to one Perfect for bed-side tables and island benches.
  • Suitable for outdoor areas.
  • Even suitable for wheelchairs and special requirements.

 

ZIGBEE - SMART DEVICES:

Zigbee devices use the lowest power consumption of WiFi, Bluetooth and Zigbee, making them suitable for batteries, with running times up to 2 years on a small button battery. Devices with batteries make installation very easy and extremely flexible.

Before installing Zigbee devices, a Zigbee Gateway needs to be installed. This will act as a bridge between your WiFi system and all Zigbee devices. The Zigbee Gateway must be connected to the Router with a data cable and connected using the App and 2.4GHz network. Once the Gateway is connected, select the Gateway on the App and push “Add device.” The devices must be put in pairing mode as indicated on the App and then added.

  •  
  • Contact Sensors - are very small, attractive, and can be placed on doors, windows or any opening system as security, or as a device to activate lights and other Smart products.
  • PIR sensors - can be easily and conveniently placed inconspicuously in rooms, hallways and areas requiring automated lighting. Two or more sensors can also be added to switch the same lights ensuring stable and reliable functioning.
  • Temperature Sensors - can be useful for sending warnings and turning on fans or other devices. Placed in a fridge, warnings can be sent if temperatures exceed 6º or in rooms to set air conditioning levels. Even in a fish tank to monitor water temperatures remotely.
  • Smoke Alarms - not only will they emit loud warning signals, but timely messages to your phone, and even the option to turn off devices. N.B. These do not replace the standard home smoke alarm but can be used in ancillary areas such as garages, sheds etc.
  • Water Sensors - any over-level or water spillage can be activate alarms and messages.

 

WiFi Cameras and Doorbells:

WiFi Cameras are very easy to install, as they only require USB power supply, or can be connected to mini solar panels if outdoors and/or run on batteries.

WiFi Cameras are extremely useful for recording visitors coming to your home as pictures are saved to the App message center. Notifications can also be sent to your Smart phone, as well as an option for Smart functions such as turning on lights or an alarm.

WiFi Cameras and doorbells have 2-way voice options, some have human detection and adjustable sensor areas, ensuring only required pictures and notifications are received.

The Doorbell cameras also have linked chimes, which are placed inside and will ring on your mobile device. These can turn on the front wall or porch, or garden lights if motion is detected.

This WiFi Garage Door Controller is extremely useful as it notifies you if your garage door is left open by mistake. Often we leave our homes and are unsure whether we have closed the door or, even worse, if the door has hit an obstruction and opened up without our knowledge.

The door can be opened and closed remotely, allowing you to open it if you are not at home. It is combined with a WiFi Camera, giving you great options and peace of mind.

A WiFi sensor can adjust various controls and settings on a Smart device. The Smart WiFi sensor combined with lights has the additional option of controlling the light brightness and even the colour temperature.

WiFi sensors give all the advantages of a good quality sensor with up to 19 meters range and 90º coverage and cost-saving options such as connecting to other Smart devices without any additional wiring. (Only live and neutral power feeds are required).

When paired with a Smart switch or even a Smart plug, a number of useful functions are available, such as on and off switching, scheduling, and notifications.

These can be easily & reliably set to ensure correct watering days and times. Soil and temperature sensor also monitors and will times and days where required to ensure ideal watering without waste.

/blog/smart-devices-connection.html.bodyHtml:
A smart home is an automated system that integrates the devices in your house, whether wired or wireless, so they can be controlled virtually from one app. That covers lights, fans, television, music system, sensors, cameras and more. Smart devices are very effective at saving energy costs, adding security, saving time and adding convenience, and they make the home more comfortable to live in.

Greenhse Technologies offers a range of smart home devices for Perth homes, including the Smart lighting products. This guide covers what to look for when buying smart devices, how to set up your router so they connect first time, and the step-by-step process for adding a device in the Tuya or Smart Life app.

Tips for purchasing smart devices

  • Choose generic apps, not proprietary ones. Products on a widely supported platform such as Tuya or Smart Life work alongside many other devices. Proprietary apps can lock you into contracts, are often more expensive, and may not be available or supported in the future.
  • Buy from local suppliers, or at least suppliers in Australia. Smart products that work in some countries are not guaranteed to work everywhere, and a local purchase comes with support, replacement and refund options.
  • Not all smart items are the same, even when they share a name and look identical. Functions are sometimes limited to save cost, and output and specifications can be lower. A good smart plug offers remote switching, multiple timers, energy monitoring and countdown options, and can be triggered by other smart devices, sensors or switches. A proprietary plug may only connect to its own brand, have limited timer control and no energy monitoring.
  • Check smart light functions. Quality smart lights offer warm to cool white and full-colour dimming, work with Alexa or Google, support timers and link to other devices. Basic models may have only simple functions and around one third of the brightness in full colour.
  • Compare cameras carefully. Resolution, recording functions and sensor capability vary greatly between smart IP cameras, and some require ongoing monthly or yearly fees.

Smart device installation tips

The main cause of connection problems is a lack of understanding of the router and how it should be set up. The second is badly written and misleading instructions. The following sections deal with both.

Router (or modem) tips

The modem converts the internet signal from your service provider, and the router sends that signal to your devices over WiFi. Most routers are dual band, using both the 2.4GHz and 5GHz frequency ranges. Unfortunately most smart devices only work on 2.4GHz, so some changes to the router are often needed before devices can be added.

Log on to the router using the details on its label, for example the address 10.1.1.1 and the password admin (or a new password you chose earlier). Open the wireless settings and make sure there is a separate 2.4GHz network.

Note that 5GHz is not the same as 5G. The terms 2.4GHz and 5GHz refer to the operating frequency of the WiFi. 5G refers to the fifth generation of mobile network, which followed 4G and 3G, and does not describe a frequency, even though each generation uses different frequencies and wavelengths.

  • If the router already has separate 2.4GHz and 5GHz networks with different names and passwords, select the 2.4GHz option (or the non-5GHz option) on your smartphone, then add the smart device using the same 2.4GHz name and password.
  • If both bands share one name and password, log on to the router, split them into two separate names and passwords, and then select the 2.4GHz option on your phone.

Also read: How To Change 5GHz To 2.4GHz To Connect Smart Devices.

The smartphone and the smart device being added must both be on the same 2.4GHz network during setup. After that, connection is straightforward in most cases. The next most common issue is making sure the device is ready for pairing and that its indicator light is flashing correctly, as described in the app.

How to add your smart device in the app

Follow these six steps, shown in the screenshots below:

  1. Set the smartphone to 2.4GHz. In the phone's WiFi settings, join the 2.4GHz network (for example Greenhouse rather than Greenhouse-5G).
  2. Open the app and tap the plus symbol in the top right hand corner to add a device.
  3. Carefully select the device being added. Check first whether it is a WiFi, Bluetooth or Zigbee product, because each type is listed separately in the categories, such as Lighting, Electrical or Security and Sensors.
  4. Set or reset the device as per the app instructions. Typically you switch the device on, hold the reset button for 5 seconds, and confirm the indicator is blinking rapidly. Complete pairing within 3 minutes of the reset.
  5. Add to 2.4GHz. Enter the WiFi password for the 2.4GHz network. The app shows a tick beside 2.4GHz and a cross beside 5GHz as a reminder that only 2.4GHz networks are supported. Tap Confirm.
  6. Wait for a successful connection. Keep the router, phone and device as close together as possible while the app finds the device, registers it to the cloud and initialises it.

Once the device is added, rename it, assign it to a room and it will be ready for schedules, scenes and voice control through Alexa or Google.

Common connection problems

  • Phone still connected to the 5GHz band, or both bands sharing one network name.
  • Wrong WiFi password entered.
  • Device not in pairing mode, or pairing timed out after 3 minutes.
  • Device too far from the router during setup.
  • Selecting the wrong device type (WiFi, Bluetooth or Zigbee) in the app.

Correct the cause, reset the device and repeat the steps. For help choosing or connecting smart devices, contact Greenhse Technologies in Perth on (08) 9297 2969 or visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069.

/blog/smart-kinetic-rf-switches.html.lede: Smart Kinetic RF switches from Greenhse Technologies are the best choice for smart homes: no wiring, no batteries and no fuss.
/blog/smart-kinetic-rf-switches.html.bodyHtml:
SMART Kinetic RF switches, offered by Greenhse Technologies, are the best choice for smart homes because of their unmatched practicality. These wireless switches need no wiring and no batteries, which makes them ideal for retrofitting existing homes. This post explains how they work, what receiver modules are available, how to pair switches to receivers, and how to set up the smart versions with your Wi-Fi.

A kinetic switch generates a tiny pulse of electricity from the press of the button itself and sends an RF signal to a receiver. Reliable, responsive RF technology means Smart Kinetic RF switches communicate through walls and obstacles, and they can be relocated or expanded as your needs change. Combined with automated scheduling on the smart receivers, they help reduce power consumption and lower electricity bills. They integrate with popular smart home ecosystems, so you can control lights through voice assistants or the mobile app. You can also watch our video, Kinetic RF Switches, for a demonstration.

Characteristics of Kinetic RF switches

  • Kinetic switches require no connected wires, or even batteries.
  • They connect directly to a receiving module placed in the ceiling near the lights or device.
  • Available in 1, 2 and 3 gang. They are attractive, very strong, neat and completely waterproof, rated IP67.
  • These switches connect to various control modules: 1000W Receiver, Dual 1200W Receiver (600W x 2), Dimmer 100W Receiver, Smart 600W Receiver and Smart Dimmer 100W Receiver.
  • Depending on the receiver module selected, Kinetic switches can turn devices on and off, dim them, and even provide SMART control.
  • With no wiring required, construction cost savings are possible. More importantly, you have complete flexibility and no limitations. Switches can be added as and where required.
  • 2-way and 3-way switching work well with this system. Multiple switches can link to one receiver, and multiple receivers can link to one switch.
  • Perfect for bedside tables and island benches, where running a cable is difficult.
  • Suitable for outdoor areas thanks to the IP67 rating.
  • Even suitable for wheelchair users and special accessibility requirements, since a switch can be mounted at any height or on any surface.

Check out our wide range of Smart Switches here.

Pairing Kinetic switches to receiver modules

The receiver module must be wired by a licensed electrician. Once it is powered, pairing takes a few seconds.

  1. Push the square linking button on the receiver until the red light flashes slowly. Let go, then push the Kinetic switch being linked once, quickly, and let go. Be careful not to push the wrong switch, because unlinking is more difficult.
  2. To unlink, push the square button for about 12 seconds. The red light flashes slowly, then flashes quickly, then stops flashing. Release the button and the switch is unlinked.

Dual receiver module

The dual receiver can connect to 2 separate devices with different switches.

  1. Connecting the first device to the first switch is the same as all receivers: push the square button for 3 seconds until the red light flashes, let go, then push the Kinetic switch once quickly and let go.
  2. To connect the second device, push the square button twice quickly and the light turns BLUE. Push and hold the square button for 3 seconds and the BLUE light flashes. Push the second Kinetic switch once quickly to pair it to the second output.
  3. To get back to the RED light, push the square button twice quickly.

Note: multiple switches can be linked to a single receiver and multiple receivers can be linked to 1 switch. Plan carefully and link correctly, or incorrect switching will occur and unlinking will be required. For the dual controller, both RED and BLUE channels may need to be unlinked.

Smart receivers

  1. SMART receivers must be linked to the home Wi-Fi. When the Smart receiver module is turned on, the red light flashes quickly.
  2. Open the Smart Life or Tuya app and push "+" to add a device.
  3. The receiver module appears in the app. Select Add device. Once added, select it and change the name.
  4. If a Smart Dimmer module has been added, set the minimum level so the light is visible at its lowest setting and there is no flickering.
  5. After a Smart receiver is added, link it to a Kinetic switch by pushing the "+ Pair" button in the app, then pushing the Kinetic switch you want to link to it once.

With Smart receivers linked to Wi-Fi and Kinetic switches, numerous options open up through the Scene function at the bottom of the app page, such as schedules, sunset timers and one-touch scenes across several rooms.

How to connect and set up Kinetic RF switches

  • Ensure your Wi-Fi is set up and working well. If you plan on using more than 10 smart devices, invest in a good Wi-Fi extender, such as the UBIQUITI U6-LR.
  • Set up a separate 2.4GHz network with its own name and password, or ask your provider or Wi-Fi supplier to set this up before they leave. Use a name and password you can remember and enter correctly each time.
  • Load and register the Smart Life or Tuya app.
  • Select the 2.4GHz Wi-Fi network on your smart device and ensure you have good signal strength where the device will be added (3 bars or more).
  • Follow the product installation instructions and use the same 2.4GHz name and password.

Overall, Smart Kinetic RF switches combine convenience, efficiency, reliability and versatility, making them the optimal choice for modern smart homes. They are available from Greenhse Technologies, the best LED lighting shop in Ellenbrook, Perth. Visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 or call (08) 9297 2969 to choose the right switches and receiver modules for your home.

/blog/smart-life-connection.html.lede: How to connect your devices using the 'SMART LIFE' app.
/blog/smart-life-connection.html.bodyHtml:
The Smart Life app is the free app used to control the WiFi lights, switches, plugs and sensors supplied by Greenhse Technologies in Perth. This guide walks through connecting a new device from start to finish: preparing your phone and router, putting the device into pairing mode, adding it in the app, and then naming it, assigning it to a room and linking it to a voice assistant.

If you prefer to follow along on screen, watch the Smart Life connection video. The written steps below cover the same process in more detail.

Before you start

  • Install the app. Download Smart Life from the App Store or Google Play, create an account with your email address and log in. Tuya Smart is the same platform and works in the same way, but keep all your devices in one app so they can be grouped and automated together.
  • Use the 2.4GHz WiFi band. Almost all smart lighting products only connect over 2.4GHz WiFi, not 5GHz. Most Perth routers are dual band. If your router shows one name for both bands, log in to the router and split them into two networks with different names (for example Home and Home-5G). Then connect your phone to the 2.4GHz network before you add any device.
  • Check the password. The app will ask for the WiFi password during pairing. Make sure you have the correct one for the 2.4GHz network.
  • Stay close to the router. During pairing, keep the phone, the router and the new device as close together as practical.

Step 1: Put the device into pairing mode

A new device is normally in pairing mode straight out of the box, shown by a rapidly flashing indicator light or, on a smart bulb or strip, by the light flashing on and off quickly. If it is not flashing, reset it as described in the product instructions. The usual methods are:

  • Smart lights and downlights: switch the light on and off at the wall three times in a row, pausing about a second between each, until it starts to flash rapidly.
  • Smart plugs and switches: hold the reset or power button for about 5 seconds until the indicator flashes quickly.
  • Sensors and other battery devices: hold the reset pin or button as shown in the manual until the LED flashes.

Rapid flashing (around twice per second) means EZ mode, which is the quick default. Slow flashing means AP mode, a fallback method covered below. Complete the next steps within about three minutes of resetting, otherwise the device will drop out of pairing mode and you will need to reset it again.

Step 2: Add the device in the app

  1. Open Smart Life and tap the plus symbol in the top right corner, then choose Add Device.
  2. Many devices will appear automatically under Discovering devices. If yours shows up, tap Add. If not, select it manually from the category list, for example Lighting, then Light Source (WiFi), or Electrical, then Socket (WiFi). Check whether the product is WiFi, Bluetooth or Zigbee before choosing, as each is listed separately and a Zigbee device needs a gateway.
  3. Confirm the WiFi network name is the 2.4GHz network and enter the password, then tap Next.
  4. Confirm that the indicator is flashing rapidly and tap Next.
  5. Wait while the progress circle runs. The app finds the device, registers it to the cloud and initialises it. This usually takes under a minute.
  6. When Added successfully appears, tap Done.

If pairing fails, the usual causes are a phone still on the 5GHz band, a mistyped password, a device that has timed out of pairing mode, or a weak signal. Fix the cause, reset the device and try again. If EZ mode keeps failing, tap Other Mode in the top right during pairing and choose AP mode: reset the device until it flashes slowly, join the temporary hotspot the device creates from your phone's WiFi settings, then return to the app to finish. The connection video shows both methods.

Step 3: Name the device and assign a room

As soon as the device is added, the app offers a pencil icon to rename it. Use a short, plain name that you will say out loud, such as Kitchen Downlights or Patio Strip, rather than the factory name. Then choose a room. Rooms are set up under Me, then Home Management, where you can create your home, add rooms and invite family members so they can control the same devices from their own phones. Assigning rooms keeps the home screen tidy and lets you switch off every light in a room with one tap or one voice command.

Step 4: Link a voice assistant

Smart Life works with Amazon Alexa and Google Home. In the Alexa app, search for the Smart Life skill, enable it and sign in with your Smart Life account. In Google Home, tap Add, then Works with Google, search for Smart Life and link the account. Once linked, every device in Smart Life appears in the assistant with the names and rooms you chose, and devices added later sync automatically. You can then say Turn off the kitchen downlights or Set the lounge to warm white, and build schedules, scenes and groups in the Smart Life app.

Quick troubleshooting checklist

  • Phone connected to 2.4GHz WiFi, with a separate network name from the 5GHz band.
  • Device flashing rapidly and added within three minutes of the reset.
  • Correct password entered, with no extra spaces.
  • Router within good range of the device.
  • Only one phone pairing the device at a time. Share access through Home Management.

Once the first device is connected the rest take only a couple of minutes each. If you get stuck, Greenhse Technologies in Perth can help. Call (08) 9297 2969 or visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069.

/blog/smart-switches-everything-you-need.h1: Crystal Glass Switches - Everything you need to know before ordering
/blog/smart-switches-everything-you-need.lede: Crystal touch switch plates and smart switches can enhance the aesthetics and functionality of a Smart Home Perth.
/blog/smart-switches-everything-you-need.bodyHtml:
Crystal touch switch plates and smart switches can enhance the aesthetics and functionality of a Smart Home Perth. These are elegant and easy to clean, with attractive soft lighting to indicate ON/OFF, and are easy to see in the dark. However, there are certain requirements and a few limitations, so please follow the guidelines below before ordering.

This post covers the two families of crystal glass switches we supply, standard touch switches and smart switches, explains the wiring each one needs, and gives practical tips for new builds and for older homes that have no neutral wire at the switch.

Standard touch switches

Standard touch switches replace an ordinary mechanical switch and are powered through the switched live wire alone, which makes them the simplest option to retrofit.

  • Standard touch switches are single-wire and do not require a neutral.
  • Available in 1, 2, 3 and 4 gang switches.
  • Two-way switching is available in 1, 2 and 3 gangs, using standard communication wiring. 2 x two-way switches will be required (any number of gangs) and these are paired electronically after installation.
  • Dimmer and non-dimmer switches on 1 plate are not available.
  • 1, 2 and 3 gang dimmers are available, but all lights on the dimmer must be dimmable.
  • With single wiring on electronic switches there can be interference from lighting circuits, and 1 x load correction device on the circuit (normally installed in the first socket) may be required.
  • Load correction devices can assist with dimming and with residual current, which causes some LED globes to glow faintly when switched off.
  • Smart lights require a load correction device on the circuit. This assists with stability and maintains the live circuit when the lights are being controlled through the app.

The reason for the load correction device is that a single-wire switch has to draw a tiny current through the light fitting to power its own electronics. LED fittings draw so little current that this can cause flicker or glow; the load correction device gives the circuit a stable path and removes the problem.

Smart switches

Smart switches carry a Wi-Fi or Bluetooth module and connect to the Smart Life app, so they can be controlled and automated as well as touched.

  • Smart switches require neutral wires.
  • 1, 2, 3 and 4 gang switches are available.
  • Curtain and blind switches are available.
  • 1 gang dimmable switches are available.
  • Smart switches are more stable because they are wired to neutral. Load correction devices are not required.
  • Smart switches can be linked to do 2-way and 3-way switching with no additional wiring.
  • Smart switches can be switched ON and OFF remotely with smart devices and can work with sensors, cameras, Alexa, Google Assistant and similar platforms.
  • Smart switches can also be linked to remote sockets or switches with no wiring.

Tips for planning your switches

  • When building a new Smart Home Perth, always allow for neutral wires or conduits wherever you may require a smart switch. It costs very little at the framing stage and a great deal after the walls are finished.
  • Smart switches are very useful at the front door, as security cameras can be linked to switches on lights for convenience and safety at no extra cost.
  • Smart switches can also enable you to add gangs and link to other switches, garden lights and so on with no extra cabling.
  • Smart switches can be combined with standard switches as they look and feel the same. This will save costs, as smart switches are not really required in most applications. A sensible approach is a smart switch at the entry, living area and outdoor lights, with standard touch switches in bedrooms and bathrooms.

What to do if you have no neutral wires or conduits

Many established Perth homes have only the switched live wires at the switch position. There are still several ways an electrician can get a neutral to the switch, or work around the lack of one:

  • Electricians can often add a neutral wire to switches on external walls, as these are frequently double brick with a cavity between the leaves.
  • Neutral wires can be added if there is a garage, cupboard or area behind the switch wall that will not be affected by running an external conduit.
  • Two-way cabling can be converted to a neutral, with correct testing and heat-shrinking the exposed cable ends to blue.
  • Circuits can be combined, and the extra cable converted to a neutral.
  • Remember that extra switches can be added using smart receivers or sockets without any wiring.

All of this work involves 240V wiring and must be carried out and tested by a licensed electrician. The options above are for discussion with your electrician, not for DIY.

Ordering your switches

Before you order, it helps to have a simple list for each switch position: how many gangs, whether it needs dimming, whether it is part of a two-way or three-way group, and whether a neutral is available. With that list, choosing between a standard touch plate and a smart plate at each location is straightforward.

After reading this, order your smart switches requirement today so that one of our Greenhse experts or recommended electricians can assist you further. Please note we can only supply recommendations, and it is advisable to discuss your options with your electrician and for them to call us direct. Greenhse Technologies is at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069, Perth, and can be reached on (08) 9297 2969.

/blog/star-light-connection-guide.html.h1: Complete LED Star Light Connection Guide
/blog/star-light-connection-guide.html.lede: Greenhse Technologies offers high-quality, energy-saving, bright LED star lights in Perth. This guide covers the transformer, controller and wiring you need to connect them.
/blog/star-light-connection-guide.html.bodyHtml:
Greenhse Technologies offers high-quality, energy-saving, bright LED Star Lights in Perth. The range covers single colour star lights in 3200K, 4000K, 5000K, 6000K and Blue, plus full-colour Smart waterproof RGBW star lights that can be set to any colour or white tone from a remote or phone app.

Coloured RGBW star lights can transform the atmosphere of a room, a hallway or an alfresco ceiling and let you tailor the lighting to your own taste. Connecting RGBW star lights is more involved than wiring single-colour star lights, because each light carries five conductors and every part of the system has to match. This guide covers the specifications and connection guidelines for star light installation, including the transformer sizes, the controller, the wiring colours and the control options.

Please read the specifications below before ordering, so you receive the correct components for the number of lights you plan to install. You can also download the Star Lights connection diagram (PDF) to keep on site.

How an RGBW star light system is put together

An RGBW star light installation has four parts, connected in this order:

  1. A 12V LED transformer (driver) plugged into a standard power point.
  2. A 3-in-1 LED controller that takes the 12V supply and drives the red, green, blue and white channels.
  3. One or more cable lines of star lights, each light spaced 1m apart along the cable.
  4. A remote, wall remote or the Tuya or Smart Life app to choose colours, brightness and scenes.

Each star light is a single piece with its own lead and sells for $16 + GST. Because the system runs on 12V DC on the light side, it is low voltage and safe to handle once the transformer is unplugged. The mains-side power point and any fixed wiring must still be installed by a licensed electrician.

Choose the right 12V transformer

One cable line can run a maximum of 6 star lights. For more than 6 lights, connect 2 or more cable lines to the controller and size the transformer to suit:

  • 12V 20W transformer, IP20, $22 + GST: runs 1 line of 6, suitable for up to 6 lights.
  • 12V 40W transformer, IP20, $35 + GST: runs 2 lines of 6, suitable for up to 12 lights.
  • 12V 75W transformer, IP20, $60 + GST: runs 4 lines of 6, suitable for up to 18 lights on three lines, with capacity for a fourth line.

IP20 means the transformer is rated for dry, indoor locations such as a ceiling space, not for exposed outdoor mounting. Keep it accessible and ventilated. Do not exceed the line and light counts above, as an overloaded transformer runs hot and shortens the life of the whole system.

Wiring the 3-in-1 controller

The controller is a MiBoxer 3-in-1 LED controller with WiFi 2.4G, and it sits between the transformer and the star lights. The wiring colours matter, so check them twice before powering up.

Input from the transformer

  • V+ to the red wire.
  • V- to the black wire.

If the input is wired incorrectly the controller will fail, and this failure is not covered by warranty.

Output to the star lights

  • Black: V+ (common positive)
  • Red: R (red channel)
  • Green: G (green channel)
  • Blue: B (blue channel)
  • White: W (white channel)

Once wired, the SET button must be selected so that the green indicator light shows on the controller. The green light confirms the controller is in the correct output mode for RGBW star lights.

Step-by-step connection

  1. Plan the layout and count the lights. Allow 1m of cable between lights and a maximum of 6 lights per line.
  2. Select the transformer: 20W for one line, 40W for two lines, 75W for up to four lines.
  3. Have your electrician install a power point in the ceiling space or cupboard where the transformer will live.
  4. Connect the transformer output to the controller input, red to V+ and black to V-.
  5. Connect each star light line to the controller output terminals, matching black, red, green, blue and white.
  6. Where you have two or more lines, join each line's five wires to the same five output terminals so every line is driven in parallel.
  7. Press SET until the green indicator light shows on the controller.
  8. Plug in the transformer and test every colour channel before closing the ceiling.

Controller and remote options

Two controller versions are available. The standard 3-in-1 controller is $15 + GST and works with the handheld and wall remotes. The 3-in-1 SMART controller is $25 + GST and adds app control through Tuya or Smart Life on a smart device or mobile phone, so you can add timers, schedules and other smart functions such as voice control.

  • RGB+CCT handheld remote, $17 + GST: colour wheel, white tone adjustment and brightness.
  • Black or white 4-zone wall remote, RGB+CCT, $35 + GST: controls up to four separate groups of star lights from one panel.
  • Tuya or Smart Life app: requires the SMART controller and a 2.4G WiFi network.

All prices above are as shown on the connection diagram and may change, so confirm current pricing when you order.

Getting help in Perth

If you are unsure how many lights, lines or transformers your ceiling needs, bring your plan to Greenhse Technologies. The Perth showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 has star lights on display, and the team can put together the transformer, controller and remote package to suit. Call (08) 9297 2969 for advice before you order.

/blog/ubiquiti-wifi-extender-setup-guide.h1: Ubiquiti WIFI Extender Setup: Complete Connection Guide
/blog/ubiquiti-wifi-extender-setup-guide.lede: What is Ubiquiti WiFi Extender? A Ubiquiti WiFi Extender is a powerful device designed to improve your wireless network's range and performance.
/blog/ubiquiti-wifi-extender-setup-guide.bodyHtml:
What is a Ubiquiti WiFi Extender? A Ubiquiti WiFi Extender is a powerful device designed to improve your wireless network's range and performance. This complete connection guide explains what the extender does, the benefits it brings to a smart home or office, and the step-by-step setup process from unboxing to switching off the WiFi on your original router.

What is a Ubiquiti WiFi Extender?

Unlike standard routers, this extender uses advanced technology to eliminate dead zones in your home or office, ensuring consistent connectivity. It is especially useful in larger spaces where the signal from your existing modem or router struggles to reach certain areas, such as a back bedroom, an upstairs office or a patio. By acting as a bridge between your router and your devices, the Ubiquiti WiFi Extender allows for uninterrupted internet access, even in challenging environments.

In practice the Ubiquiti unit is a ceiling-mounted access point. It is fed by a data cable from your existing modem or router, and it broadcasts a new, stronger wireless signal from the centre of the building. Your phones, laptops, smart switches, cameras and other WiFi devices then connect to the Ubiquiti rather than to the router tucked away in a corner.

Benefits of using a Ubiquiti WiFi Extender

Using a Ubiquiti WiFi Extender offers several benefits, particularly for users with high internet demands.

  • Far more devices. It significantly boosts the number of devices that can connect simultaneously, from about 12 to up to 300. This makes it ideal for smart homes or offices where multiple devices are constantly in use. A typical home with smart lighting, smart switches, cameras, TVs, phones and tablets can quickly exceed what a standard modem router handles well.
  • Stronger signal and speed. It enhances signal strength and speed, providing a seamless experience for streaming, gaming or video conferencing.
  • Dual-band support. It supports dual-band frequencies (2.4GHz and 5GHz), ensuring flexibility and compatibility with various devices. Most smart lighting products and smart switches use 2.4GHz, which travels further through walls, while laptops and phones can use the faster 5GHz band.
  • Better coverage from a central position. With its central placement under the ceiling, the extender ensures optimal signal distribution throughout your space, rather than the signal having to fight its way from one end of the house to the other.

Watch the video for a hassle-free guide to connecting your Ubiquiti WiFi Extender. The steps below follow the same order.

How to connect a Ubiquiti WiFi Extender

  1. Unbox the device. Remove the device from its packaging and ensure you have all the necessary components, including power adapters and cables. Ubiquiti uses P.O.E (Power Over Ethernet), which means the unit receives both power and data through the single network cable, so you will require the correct P.O.E power supply. There is no separate power lead at the ceiling.
  2. Connect to power and data. Connect a data cable from the original modem or router to the P.O.E adapter, then run the data cable from the adapter to the Ubiquiti device. Ideally, place the device centrally in your home, under the ceiling. Data cables are usually run through the ceiling space, which keeps the installation tidy and puts the access point where its signal spreads evenly.
  3. Prepare for installation. Before installing, take a clear picture of the barcode on the back of the Ubiquiti device, as you will need it later for app configuration. Once the unit is mounted on the ceiling the barcode is out of sight.
  4. Install the Ubiquiti app. Download and open the Ubiquiti app on your phone. Select "Add Device" and scan the barcode when prompted. The app will find the unit on your network and register it.
  5. Configure the device. Once added, configure the WiFi name and password for both the 2.4GHz and 5GHz frequencies.
  6. Optimise device settings. If multiple devices are already connected to your existing router, use the same WiFi name and password for the Ubiquiti extender to maintain continuity. Your smart lights, switches and other devices will then reconnect automatically without needing to be set up again.
  7. Disable the original WiFi. After setup, switch off the WiFi on your original modem or router to fully utilise the extender's capabilities. This stops devices from clinging to the weaker router signal and ensures everything connects through the Ubiquiti.

Practical notes

  • The modem or router still does its job of connecting to the internet. Only its wireless broadcast is turned off; the cable to the Ubiquiti carries everything else.
  • If a data cable needs to be run through the ceiling and terminated at a wall plate, a licensed cabler should do the work.
  • Keep the photo of the barcode. If you ever reset the device or change phones you can add it again quickly.

Wrap-up

With the Ubiquiti WiFi Extender you can enjoy enhanced internet connectivity and seamless operation of your smart devices, with capacity for hundreds of connections and a strong signal in every room. Visit the showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069, or call (08) 9297 2969, to talk about WiFi coverage and smart lighting for your home or office.

Strip lighting is one of the most versatile lighting solutions available, creating architectural features while delivering practical light. No single strip does everything, which is why more than 40 types exist. This Greenhse Technologies Perth guide covers the six factors that decide which strip lighting suits your space, then the product families we stock.

1. Length and run capability

Run length decides the voltage.

  • 12V strip: higher current, shorter runs, small applications.
  • 24V strip: lower current and less heat, typically up to 5 metres per run.
  • Long-run 24V strip: up to 20 metres from one end or 40 metres powered from both ends, no visible voltage drop.
  • 240V strip: very long runs up to 50 metres, minimal voltage drop, lower heat, no driver required.

2. Colour options

  • RGB (full colour): millions of colours, though white is mixed and often looks less natural.
  • CCT (tunable white): adjustable white, typically 2700K to 6500K, where flexibility is needed.
  • Single colour: consistent quality white in 2700K (warm), 3000K (warm white), 4000K (neutral) or 5500K to 6000K (cool or daylight).

For quality white choose single colour or CCT; for effects choose RGB.

3. Brightness and performance

Brightness is measured in lumens, not watts. More wattage generally means more light, but efficiency matters more: 150 lumens per watt or better gives more light for a lower power bill. Greenhse strips range from 7.5W/m with 700 lumens to 23W/m with over 3500 lumens per metre (a standard 8 to 10Watt downlight is about 900 lumens). Entry level is around 700 lumens/m, high performance 3500+ lumens/m. Display lighting and niches need high brightness; under-cabinet runs of 2 to 3 metres suit about 12W/m with 1800+ lumens/m. All strip lights can be dimmed for efficiency and control.

4. Quality matters

  • LED density: higher density means smoother, dot-free light.
  • CRI: CRI 90+ renders accurate, vibrant colours; CRI 70 is lower quality.
  • PCB construction: 10mm PCB is stronger than 5mm; 3 OZ copper layers handle heat better and last longer.
  • Efficiency: 160 lm/W uses far less power than 80 lm/W.
  • Voltage: 24V runs cooler and outlasts 12V.
  • Coatings and chip design: add durability and weather resistance and prevent light separation.
  • Warranty: up to 5 years on premium strips.

5. Controllers and smart control

Single colour strip needs no controller (dimming modules are optional). CCT needs one for colour temperature, RGB for colour selection and effects. Control options: handheld remotes, wall switches, smartphone apps, voice control through Google or Alexa, sensors and automation systems.

6. Channels and installation

Aluminium channels improve heat dissipation, extend lifespan, diffuse light and give a premium architectural finish. Recessed wing channels build into cabinetry; surface-mounted suit retrofits. Finishes: aluminium, or premium black and white. Diffusers give 15% to 20% diffusion to cut glare and hide LED dots.

Choosing the right LED strip light

Our most common LED strip lighting products are all certified, high quality and budget friendly.

240V strip lighting

Best for continuous runs up to 50 metres from one supply. Low heat means no aluminium profile, no transformer and less wiring, with even colour and brightness over the full length and a tough TPU finish. RGB has full colour control and dimming with a choice of remotes; single colour can be Triac dimmable; an RGB gateway or smart dimming module adds smart control. Applications: recessed ceilings, large architectural lighting. Options: RGB, 3000K warm white, 4000K natural white, 6000K daylight.

Long-run 24V COB

Dotless COB strip running 20 metres from one end or 40 metres from both ends with no voltage drop. Thin, with short cut lengths and connectors that avoid waste up to 4 metres. Low power at 7.5W/m in IP20 or IP67 silicon injected. Applications: cabinetry, balustrades, hidden recesses, outdoors. Options: IP20 3000K, IP20 4000K, IP67 3000K.

24V RGB COB

Very bright dotless full colour with a good cool white from RGB White. Runs 5 metres, or 10 metres with both ends connected, with connectors for lengths up to 2 metres. High power at 16W/m, so needs an aluminium profile. Applications: kitchens, bars, shelving, feature recesses. Options: IP20 16W/m, IP65 15W/m with heat-shrink.

Display strip lighting 24V 23W/m

About 3800 lumens per metre, CRI above 90 for vibrant product colours, 165 lumens per watt.

24V CCT COB

Very bright dotless light adjustable from warm to cool white (2700K to 6500K). Runs 5 metres, or 10 metres from both ends, 2 metre connectors, 16W/m, aluminium profile required. Applications: under kitchen cabinets, cabinetry, bars, bulkheads, shelving, architectural features.

24V RGB SMD

High-density, stable full colour for outdoors. Runs 5 metres, or 10 metres from both ends, 16W/m, no profile needed. Applications: gardens, outdoor areas, facades, pools, water features. Options: IP67 silicon injected 16W/m, IP65 gel coated.

24V high lumen SMD

Very efficient and bright, strongest build, lifespan over 50 000 hours on a 3 OZ strip. The 12W/m option needs no aluminium channel. Runs 5 metres, or 10 metres from both ends, 2 metre connectors. Applications: under cabinets, display lighting, bathroom niches, retail. Options: IP20 23W/m CRI>90 in 4000K and warm white; IP65 silicon gel 20W/m in 4000K and 5500K; IP65 silicon gel 12W/m in 3000K, 4000K and 5500K.

Neon IP67 strip

Fully programmable colour strip for signage, feature outlines and commercial installations. Runs 5 metres from one end, power supplied every 10 metres, a data cable links multiple strips, Bluetooth controllers (no wifi needed), 12x12mm aluminium support profile. Options: RGB 12x12mm side bend in 5m and 3m; RGB 6x12mm side bend in 5m and 3m; CCT 6x12mm side bend in 10m, 5m and 3m; 3000K warm white 6x12mm side bend in 10m, 5m and 3m.

Final thoughts

Choosing strip lighting comes down to three questions: how long is the run, what colour flexibility do you need, and how bright must the space be. Answer those and the choice is simple. Done well, strip lighting does not just illuminate a space, it transforms it. Visit Greenhse Technologies, your local LED lighting store at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069, or call (08) 9297 2969.

What is a low-glare downlight?

A low-glare downlight is a recessed LED light designed to minimise direct glare while delivering focused, effective illumination. Standard downlights often expose the LED source directly. Low-glare models use deeper recessed lenses, specialised diffusers or controlled beam angles so you see the lit room rather than a bright disc in the ceiling.

Why glare matters

Glare occurs when a light source is far brighter than its surroundings. It leads to eye fatigue, reduced visibility, reflections on televisions and computer screens, visual distraction and reduced room ambience. In homes it makes living rooms, bedrooms, home offices and entertainment areas less comfortable. In commercial settings it affects productivity and customer experience. Choosing low glare downlights creates a softer, more balanced environment with sufficient brightness.

Benefits of low-glare downlights

  • Improved visual comfort: less direct exposure to bright LED chips means less eye strain, particularly where lights stay on for long periods.
  • Better light distribution: engineered optics and beam angles spread light evenly and remove harsh hotspots.
  • Reduced screen reflections: televisions, laptops, tablets and phones show fewer reflections, improving viewing comfort.
  • Enhanced aesthetics: the recessed source lets the fitting blend into the ceiling and highlights the room rather than the light.

Where to use them

Living rooms, where relaxing, entertaining, television and reading all happen. Bedrooms, where soft light supports relaxation. Home offices, where extended screen use makes glare a real problem. Dining areas, for a warm, inviting atmosphere. Hotels and hospitality venues, where premium projects use low-glare lighting for guest comfort and a luxurious feel.

Low-glare downlights vs standard downlights

Standard downlights may appear brighter at first, but low-glare models provide a superior overall lighting experience by balancing brightness with comfort.

/blog/what-do-you-need-to-make-you-home-.bodyHtml:
Smart homes have become quite popular in Perth. A smart home makes your life easier and more efficient, letting you remotely control your home lighting and other home essentials from your phone or by voice. If you want to make your home smart, this blog explains what you need: the two basics every smart-ready home requires, what makes a good WiFi system, how to choose a smart platform, how to choose products, and the difference between WiFi, Bluetooth and Zigbee devices.

To make your home smart or smart-ready, you only need 2 things

  1. A good WiFi system.
  2. Neutral wires to your switches. There are solutions for homes without neutral wires, although with neutral wires the costs are lower, switches are more stable and the options are simpler.

A neutral wire at the switch matters because a smart switch is a small computer that needs constant power to stay connected to your network. With active and neutral present it can power itself without interfering with the light circuit. If you are building or renovating, ask your electrician to run a neutral to every switch plate; it is a cheap step at framing stage and expensive to add later.

What is a good WiFi system?

A good WiFi system gives you good coverage throughout your entire home and even the outside areas where smart products may be needed. It also needs to be quick and allow sufficient devices to be connected. This prevents slow functioning of smart devices and, even more importantly, prevents them from disconnecting and not functioning at all.

A standard home router is not designed to manage a smart home. The signal will not be strong, and generally the maximum number of 2.4GHz devices it can connect to is 12. It also does not manage the signal optimally between devices; instead it divides the bandwidth 12 times and becomes extremely slow.

There are many devices available. From experience, the range that works best is Ubiquiti. The Ubiquiti U6-LR is a single device that can control a complete home. One carefully positioned unit can cover a double-storey home inside and out. For larger homes, or areas further from the extender, a second Ubiquiti or even a simple WiFi booster can provide a stronger signal.

These devices are designed to be positioned under the ceiling, centrally in the home, and connect to the router with a data cable using POE (power over ethernet), so no power point is needed at the access point. This data cable must be allowed for when building a new home, with multiple data points for larger or double-storey homes.

Setting up the WiFi extender

  • Select separate 2.4GHz and 5GHz networks, with passwords you can remember correctly. Most smart devices only connect on 2.4GHz, so a separate network name avoids confusion.
  • If you choose the same name and password as your original router, disable the WiFi on the original router once the extender is connected to the data cable. All your devices will continue to work without resetting them, and they will work better.

Selecting the smart platform

Many suppliers propose systems with exorbitant costs and, even worse, discontinued or outdated systems that will not be supported in the future. In fact, it is quite simple and not expensive. There are a number of proprietary systems on the market, some from good companies, but that does not make them the best solution. /blog/what-is-free-home-battery-storage-.bodyHtml:
The Australian Federal Government has announced a $2.3 billion investment in home battery systems. The aim is to support Australia's transition to clean energy and ease demand on the national electricity grid by helping households store the solar power they generate during the day and use it in the evening. For many homes the rebate is large enough to cover the entire cost of the battery, which is why it is being described as free home battery storage for Australians.

This post explains how the rebate works, what it could be worth to you, and how the Greencharge GH-B16 large-format battery from Greenhse Technologies fits into the program. Read more on the Federal Government Cheaper Home Battery Program page.

How the rebate works

Homeowners can now access rebates of up to $370 per kWh of battery capacity for batteries certified by the Clean Energy Council. The incentive is delivered through Small-Scale Technology Certificates (STCs), the same mechanism that has supported rooftop solar for years. STCs are created when an eligible system is installed and are normally assigned to the installer or retailer, who passes the value on as an upfront discount on the quoted price. You do not need to apply separately or wait for a cheque.

The rebate is not fixed. It will gradually reduce from July 2025 through July 2030, so the earlier a system is installed, the higher the discount. Read more on STCs to see how the certificate value is calculated.

What a home battery actually does

A solar system without storage exports surplus energy to the grid during the day, usually for a small feed-in credit, and then buys power back at a much higher rate at night. A battery captures that surplus and releases it after sunset, so more of your own solar is used at home. Larger capacity means more evening and overnight demand can be covered, and it also allows the battery to take part in grid support programs.

Why choose Greenhse Technologies?

Greenhse Technologies has secured premium large-format batteries designed for maximum efficiency and reliability. The systems are available in 16, 32 and 48 kWh sizes and qualify for rebates that can cover the entire cost of the battery. A 16 kWh unit suits a typical family home with solar, while 32 and 48 kWh configurations suit larger homes, homes with electric vehicles or pool heating, and households that want to maximise their return from the rebate and from virtual power plant participation.

Installation is available in the Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth metro areas.

How the GH-B16 battery system works

The Greencharge GH-B16 Battery is:

  • VPP (Virtual Power Plant) ready: energy providers can tap into stored energy when demand on the grid peaks, and pay you for it.
  • Compatible with most low-voltage hybrid inverters: it can usually be connected to an existing solar inverter, making installation seamless.

This means you benefit in two ways:

  • Upfront savings of up to $17,760 ($370 x 48 kWh) through the rebate.
  • Ongoing returns of up to $750 per year from VPP participation, depending on your system and location.

That is a potential $2,000 to $2,600 per battery in added value over time, on top of the everyday savings from using your own stored solar instead of buying grid power at peak rates.

What is a virtual power plant?

A VPP links many home batteries together under software control. When the grid is under stress, for example on a hot summer evening in Perth, the energy provider can draw a small amount from each battery and pay the owners for it. Your home keeps a reserve, and the arrangement is managed automatically through the inverter and battery management system.

Why the Greenhse GH-B16 is different

Many battery systems are built by combining smaller cells or modules to reach a larger capacity. The GH-B16 is a specialist large-format battery, purpose-built for durability and performance, with fewer cells and fewer connections to manage. Key benefits include:

  • Highest-grade lithium, fully documented from source to final assembly.
  • Advanced Battery Management System that balances and regulates the cells for longer life and safety.
  • Built-in safety features protecting your home and the system.
  • 8000+ life cycles with a 10-year warranty. One cycle is a full charge and discharge, so 8000 cycles covers well beyond a decade of daily use.
  • Wide inverter compatibility, or upgrade to a 10 kW inverter at a reduced cost if your existing inverter is not suitable.

Battery installation must be carried out by a licensed electrician with the appropriate accreditation, and the system must be Clean Energy Council certified to qualify for the STC rebate. Greenhse arranges compliant installation as part of the package.

Is it right for your home?

A home battery makes the most sense when you already have solar, or are installing it at the same time, and when a good share of your electricity is used in the evening. Points to check before you commit:

  • Your current inverter model and whether it is a low-voltage hybrid unit.
  • Your daily energy use and how much of it falls outside daylight hours.
  • Whether you want to join a VPP for the extra annual return.
  • Timing, because the rebate steps down each year from July 2025 to July 2030.

With Greenhse, you are not just installing a battery. You are investing in energy independence, lower bills and a smarter grid. Visit the Greencharge website and select HOME BATTERY to learn more, or contact Greenhse Technologies in Perth on (08) 9297 2969 or at the showroom, 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069, to discuss the right battery size for your home.

/blog/why-are-dc-fans-better-than-ac-fan.h1: Why are DC Fans better than AC Fans?
/blog/why-are-dc-fans-better-than-ac-fan.lede: As time goes by, upgrading yourself and the things around you is essential.
/blog/why-are-dc-fans-better-than-ac-fan.bodyHtml:
As time goes by, upgrading yourself and the things around you is essential. There are many types of ceiling fans available on the market, and we have found that Australian households are often confused about selecting the right fan for their needs. This article covers why DC fans are better than AC fans, how the two motor types differ, what the difference means for running costs, noise and installation, and what to look for when choosing a ceiling fan for your Perth home.

What is the difference between AC and DC fans?

DC stands for direct current and AC stands for alternating current. The names describe the type of electricity the motor runs on. Residential properties are supplied with AC power, which is why ceiling fans have traditionally featured AC motors: the motor simply runs straight off the mains.

A DC fan still connects to the same 240V household supply, but it contains a small built-in converter that changes AC into DC before it reaches the motor. A DC motor uses permanent magnets and electronic control rather than the copper windings of an AC induction motor. This is the reason it can spin at precisely controlled speeds while drawing very little power.

Although AC fans are cheaper to manufacture, they are less energy-efficient than DC fans. The difference shows up on the power bill every month for the life of the fan.

Quiet, low-cost cooling for bedrooms

Purchasing a DC fan for a bedroom gives you extremely quiet cooling at the lowest running cost. A DC fan can be up to 8 times cheaper to run than an AC fan and up to 50 times cheaper than ducted air conditioning. The only noise is the sound of the airflow. There are no buzzing motors, which softens the external noise of your environment and contributes to better sleep and health.

Comparison between AC fans and DC fans

  • Running cost: AC fans are up to 85% more expensive to run. A 35W DC fan can produce the same airflow as a 60W AC fan. The AC fan will always draw 60 watts, whereas a DC fan will draw as low as 7W on the lower setting, which is the setting used most frequently, saving up to 88% in running costs.
  • Noise: AC fan motors are noisy. At night in a bedroom you will hear the motor hum, whereas a DC fan has no motor noise.
  • Installation: AC fans need in-wall controllers, which are more expensive to install. DC fans can be connected to normal wall switches, with speed and direction handled by the remote.
  • Speed options: AC fans have limited speed options, normally 3. DC fans have 6 speed options on the remote, as well as a reversible option for winter.
  • Lifespan: AC fans do not last as long as DC fans, which have warranties of 6 years.

Advantages of DC fans

  • Much cheaper to run
  • Cheaper and quicker to install
  • Quiet motor
  • More fan speed options
  • Reversible fan for winter
  • Long lifespan, backed by a 6 year warranty

The reverse function deserves a mention. In summer the fan pushes air downwards to create a cooling breeze on your skin. In winter, running the fan in reverse at low speed gently pulls air upwards and pushes the warm air that collects at the ceiling back down the walls, so a heated room feels more even without the draught.

Choosing the right DC ceiling fan

Greenhse Technologies has a large range of DC ceiling fans in Perth in different styles and colours. Aesthetics and personal choice seem to be the biggest influence when selecting a fan. However, wind flow rate and ceiling height are the most important factors.

  • Airflow: match the fan size and airflow rating to the room. A large living area or alfresco needs a bigger blade span and higher airflow than a small bedroom.
  • Ceiling height: blades need clearance above the floor to work safely and effectively. We have fans with very low depth for low ceilings, so a standard-height room still gets good airflow.
  • Integrated light: we stock fans with 24-watt high brightness lights to suit a single room without compromise, dimmable and colour selectable with the remote, so the fan can replace the room's main light.
  • Smart control: full smart fans can be run from your phone or by voice, and scheduled to switch off after you fall asleep.

Whichever model you choose, the electrical connection must be carried out by a licensed electrician. Because a DC fan wires to a normal wall switch and does not need an in-wall controller, that job is usually quick and inexpensive.

The logical choice for modern homes

Thanks for reading our blog. We hope you now understand why DC fans are the more logical choice for modern homes today: lower running costs, silent operation, six speeds, a winter reverse mode and a 6 year warranty. To see the range and feel the airflow for yourself, visit Greenhse Technologies at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069, or phone (08) 9297 2969 and our Perth team will help you pick the right fan for each room.

/blog/why-choose-24v-strip-light.html.bodyHtml:
There are many types and styles of 24V strip lighting available at the Greenhse store in Perth. We have selected the latest styles to give you the best lighting effects to complement and improve your home or commercial application. This post explains what professional 24V LED strip lighting is, why 24V is the better choice over 12V, and what to look for when you specify a strip for a kitchen, stairway, ceiling recess or outdoor area.

24V professional LED strip lighting

24V LED strip lighting is designed to supply long, seamless lighting to homes and commercial installations. It provides complete, even light with the best aesthetics, without the hot spots or dark gaps you get from cheaper strips. It is often called architectural lighting, because the strip is usually hidden in a small niche, recess, pelmet or aluminium channel so that only the lighting effect is seen, not the light source itself.

Strip lighting can be exceptionally bright, up to 4500 lumens per metre, and very versatile. It is used indoors under kitchen benches and inside joinery, and outdoors along eaves, steps and garden walls. It is available in numerous colour options, brightnesses and lengths, so the same product family can light a display shelf softly or replace a fluorescent tube in a workshop.

We constantly update the strip range to offer the best value and product, so some specifications may change from batch to batch. Check the current product page before ordering.

Why 24V beats 12V

A strip light is a chain of LEDs mounted on a flexible circuit board and powered by a low-voltage DC driver. At 24V the driver only needs to push half the current through the strip to deliver the same wattage as a 12V strip. Lower current means:

  • Less heat generated in the copper tracks and LEDs, so the strip runs cooler.
  • Less voltage drop along the length, so the far end of the strip is as bright as the near end.
  • Longer runs from a single feed point, which means fewer drivers and fewer joins.
  • A longer lifespan, because heat is the main thing that shortens LED life.

24V has half the current and heat of 12V, and therefore double the lifespan. It also allows runs of up to 10m from one end, double the length of a 12V strip, which makes it far easier to light a long kitchen bench or a whole ceiling perimeter without visible breaks.

Main feature highlights of 24V LED strip lights

  • High output of up to 4500 lumens per metre, brighter than fluorescent tubes.
  • Very high density, up to 240 LEDs per metre SMD or 505 LEDs COB, creating bright, dotless strip lighting effects.
  • 24V has half the current and heat of 12V, therefore double the lifespan.
  • Long lifespan of up to 50,000 hours when used with an aluminium profile or channel.
  • Runs of up to 10m from one end, double the length of a 12V strip.
  • A choice of colour temperatures: warm, natural or bright white, or vibrant 16 million colours from RGB full-colour strip.
  • Rich, deep colour depth with high colour rendering up to CRI 90.
  • Dimmable and adjustable with control modules, remotes and smart devices.

SMD versus COB

SMD strip uses individual surface-mounted LED chips spaced along the board. At 240 LEDs per metre the chips are so close that the light merges into a continuous line. COB (chip on board) strip mounts many tiny LEDs under a continuous phosphor coating, so a 505 LED COB strip gives a completely smooth glow with no dots even when it is not behind a diffuser.

Colour temperature and CRI

Warm white (around 3000K) suits bedrooms and living areas, natural white (around 4000K) suits kitchens and bathrooms, and bright white (5000K and above) suits garages and task areas. CRI (colour rendering index) describes how accurately a light shows colours compared with daylight; a CRI 90 strip makes timber, stone and food look natural rather than washed out.

Channels, diffusers and drivers

Various channel types with diffusers are available in 3m lengths. An aluminium channel does three jobs: it acts as a heat sink, which is why the 50,000 hour lifespan is quoted with a profile; it protects the strip from knocks and dust; and its diffuser evens the light so no LED dots show. Surface, recessed and corner profiles cover most joinery and plasterboard details.

Every 24V strip needs a matching 24V DC driver sized to the total wattage of the run, and dimmable, CCT or RGB strips need a compatible control module or smart controller. Any 240V wiring to the driver must be carried out by a licensed electrician; the low-voltage strip side can then be fitted by the installer or cabinet maker.

Where to see the range in Perth

Have a look at our range of Decorative LED Strip Lights online, or visit the Greenhse Technologies showroom at 5/1 Locke Lane, Ellenbrook WA 6069 to compare strip brightness, colour temperature and channel options in person. Call (08) 9297 2969 for help with driver sizing, run lengths and controllers for your project.

The LED downlight market is extremely competitive. As a result manufacturers are making cheap downlights and are compromising on quality to compete in the market. This post explains how Greenhse Technologies has approached the same price pressure differently, with a new low-profile 8W LED downlight that cuts cost by removing parts you do not need rather than by lowering the quality of the parts you do.

Greenhse Technologies has been in operation for almost 2 decades and is a reputable and trusted LED lighting supplier in Perth. We are committed to providing you with the highest quality, technically advanced LED lighting products at wholesale prices. Quality is always guaranteed.

How we lowered the cost without lowering the quality

In order to compete in this low-cost market we have come up with a new solution that enables us to supply a high-quality LED downlight with a long 50 000hr lifespan, all at a lower cost. The savings come from the design of the fitting and the way it is packed and installed:

  • We have made the downlight smaller to reduce material cost.
  • We have eliminated the need for a GPO, which would cost $1.20 or more per light.
  • We have eliminated the cord and plug on the downlight, saving further cost.
  • The downlights take up one third of the space of normal downlights with sockets.
  • This reduces shipping costs and, more importantly, saves you storage space on site and in the van.
  • There is no need to connect sockets and secure them to beams, which saves installation time. No screws, just a simple quick connect with a secondary loop for connecting multiple lights in a run.

For an electrician wiring a whole house, removing the plug and socket from every downlight adds up. Each light is terminated directly with the quick connector, and the secondary loop lets the next light in the room be fed from the previous one without going back to a junction box.

Specifications and performance

The Greenhse Technologies new 8W low-profile cost saver also has high CRI, high lumen output and a long lifespan. It offers good heat dissipation with no flickering and no UV, a built-in driver, TRIAC dimmable operation and a beam angle of 120º for a wide, even spread of light.

High CRI (colour rendering index) means colours in the room look natural rather than washed out, which matters in kitchens, retail displays and anywhere skin tones are viewed. TRIAC dimming means the light works with common leading-edge and trailing-edge wall dimmers, so no special control gear is required. The power factor of PF≥0.9 indicates the driver draws current efficiently, which keeps the load on the circuit low and is a sign of a well-designed driver.

The fitting is recommended for homes, offices, retail, schools, supermarkets and similar spaces. With a depth of only 40mm it is good for areas with shallow ceilings where a standard downlight and its driver will not fit above the plasterboard. It is also a good choice for public areas such as stairways, reception areas and corridors that are lit for long hours and benefit from the 50 000hr lifespan.
